knowledge: round 1: the knowledge as merged on main at 0ddfd1c, every one of the 641 items, in its q_reworded (bank: first wording)
how: scripts/eval/seat_exam_sweep.mjs: seat stood in for by a model on the subscription, given the settled facts and six sources (expected entries + BM25 neighbours, 2,400 characters each); graded by code (canon, facts, figures), then by the calibrated judge for what code could not decide

items.wording: Is our marketplace one big network where every new user helps everyone?
items.answer: No. A two-sided marketplace has a cross-side network effect, but in B2B procurement it is local, not global: a waterproofing supplier adds value only to buyers who need waterproofing. So QuotesDone has one network per trade, and each must reach liquidity on its own; we measure liquidity per trade and emirate because response differs by site. Local networks are easier to start and easier for a competitor to copy cell by cell, and multi-homing weakens each of them. Data network effects are real but weaker and slower. So we never claim 'we have network effects' in aggregate, and a cell below liquidity is not yet defensible.

items.wording: A buyer wants us to hold the money until the job is done. Should we start doing that?
items.answer: No, not on my authority. QuotesDone is lightly managed: it verifies suppliers, matches the trade, collects comparable quotes and charges a reveal fee; it does not hold the customer's money, execute the contract or guarantee the work, and we hold no money for the job (no escrow). Holding funds would change the company's legal role, so escrow is the founder's decision. What I bring him is evidence: does it lift reveal conversion or cut leakage by more than it costs per reveal. A managed step is added only when that evidence exists. I would tell the buyer politely that this is not part of our model today.

items.wording: We burned AED 200k to add AED 50k of new annual revenue. Is that efficient?
items.answer: No. Burn multiple is net burn divided by net new annualised net revenue: 200k / 50k = 4. David Sacks' bands are under 1 amazing, 1 to 1.5 great, 1.5 to 2 good, 2 to 3 suspect and above 3 bad, so 4 is bad. A quarter above 3 triggers cutting the least efficient spend line first. Two cautions: the denominator must be reveal fees plus subscriptions after refunds, times 12 for a month, not a booked figure; and before launch the multiple is undefined, so we then report runway in months instead. I assume the AED 200k is net burn; the question does not say.

items.wording: If someone invests half a million at a two million valuation before the money, what stake does he get?
items.answer: He gets 20%. Post-money equals pre-money plus new cash: AED 2,000,000 + AED 500,000 = AED 2,500,000. His ownership is the investment divided by post-money: 500,000 / 2,500,000 = 20%. Every existing holder is diluted by that same 20% proportion, so the founder drops from 100% to 80%. If an option pool were created before the round it would dilute only the existing holders. I would only model this for the founder; fundraising is founder-reserved, and I never quote a valuation or percentage to anyone else.
items.note: 20% and founder at 80%; correct arithmetic

items.wording: How do I show the subscription money in the monthly numbers?
items.answer: As a bridge of its four movements, never one number: new, expansion, contraction and churned MRR, with MRR the normalised monthly value of active subscriptions and ARR it times 12. But note the facts: supplier registration is free permanently for the first 1,000 businesses, and AED 1,000 a year applies only from the 1,001st, so subscription revenue is separate from the reveal-fee engine and kept out of the headline plan. Until measured it is shown as 'not measured', not estimated. Retention is measured by monthly cohort. Founder transfers are capital, never revenue, and only collected, reconciled money counts.
items.note: four-movement bridge and monthly cohort retention both stated

items.wording: Existing subscribers paid us more this year than last even after cancellations. What does that tell us?
items.answer: That net revenue retention is above 100%: NRR includes expansion, so above 100% means the existing base grows on its own even after cancellations. Check it against gross revenue retention, which excludes expansion and can never exceed 100%, to see whether churn is hidden behind upgrades. Report MRR as a bridge (new, expansion, contraction, churned) and by monthly cohort so a good month cannot hide a churn problem. Caveat for us: supplier subscriptions start only from the 1,001st registration (the first 1,000 are free permanently), so this is a future reading; today it would be 'not measured'.

items.wording: What should I expect in the monthly pack you send me?
items.answer: A pack you can read in ten minutes, sent three to five days before the review. It has six parts: a one-page summary of what happened, what is on or off plan and the decisions requested; KPIs against plan with each variance explained; financials (profit and loss, cash, burn and runway); progress on the year's milestones; the top risks with owners and mitigations; and the decisions needed, each with options, a recommendation and evidence. Money lines come from the accountant's reconciled books, a metric not yet measured is shown as 'not measured', and the pack ends with explicit decisions that are written into the decision log with a re-check date.

items.wording: A supplier wants a written guarantee signed by us. Can the CEO software seat sign it?
items.answer: No. A seat cannot sign a guarantee for the company. Only the LLC manager binds it: the founder is owner and manager, and the seats act under his authority. A seat that commits the company outside that authority creates a liability he personally carries, and managers are liable for fraud, breach of law and mismanagement. Anything that commits the company, such as a contract, bank mandate, guarantee or hire, needs the manager's signature, and I keep a record of which document carries it. So I would prepare the request with the facts and put it to the founder, who decides.
items.note: Says the LLC manager binds the company; rubric says QuotesDone is a sole establishment and LLC manager rules do not apply; written-authority route missing

items.wording: Which kind of lasting advantage can a small marketplace like ours realistically start with?
items.answer: Counter-positioning against traditional tendering and directories (instant, free to ask, pay only on reveal), and local network economies per trade. Helmer's seven powers are scale economies, network economies, counter-positioning, switching costs, branding, cornered resource and process power, and they arrive in sequence: counter-positioning and cornered resource matter at origination, network and scale economies in takeoff, branding and process power at stability. Switching costs and brand come later. Decision rule: every strategic initiative must name the power it builds and its barrier; one that builds no power is operational, not strategic. Network effects are never claimed in aggregate, only per liquid trade cell.

items.wording: When a contractor posts a request, what is he really trying to get done?
items.answer: His functional job is to get several comparable, compliant quotations from licensed suppliers quickly, without chasing anyone. The emotional job is not being overcharged or embarrassed by a bad supplier. He is hiring QuotesDone in place of what he uses today: WhatsApp groups, personal contacts, directories, tender portals or his own vendor list, and the real competitor can be doing nothing. So every product, pricing and marketing proposal is framed as the job it serves and the current hire it replaces, and research asks about the last time he did the job, not opinions on features.

items.wording: Can we put the SME fund money into next year's numbers?
items.answer: Not yet. Treat anything unconfirmed as zero in the forecast. Routes like Dubai SME or the Khalifa Fund exist, but current eligibility (several programmes are limited to UAE nationals), amounts and terms, and whether a single-owner mainland LLC with no revenue qualifies, are not verified. The rule: read the programme's current published terms on its own site, record eligibility as a measured yes or no, and only then count it. It would also never be revenue: reported numbers must not present unmeasured figures or pipeline as signed, and the founder's own transfers are capital. Capital decisions are the founder's.

items.wording: A report says we did two million last month. Is that what we earned?
items.answer: Not necessarily. The word has three meanings: requested value (what buyers posted), revealed value (the quotes buyers chose and paid to reveal) and net revenue (the 3% reveal fee actually collected, less refunds). GMV is not revenue. A report saying two million without naming which is unusable; I state every headline as a triple of requested, revealed and collected. If AED 2M were revealed value, the fee would be about AED 60,000 (3% x 2,000,000), before refunds. Only collected revenue reconciled to the bank by the accountant counts toward the plan scenarios, and the owner's transfers are capital, never income.
items.note: GMV is not revenue; revenue is collected fee less refunds; 60,000 is correct arithmetic

items.wording: How much do we spend to win one paying customer, and how do we count it?
items.answer: Count it per side. Buyer CAC is acquisition spend divided by customers acquired; only the demand side pays, so that is the paying customer. The plan's paid benchmark of about AED 250 per posted request becomes about AED 1,956 per revealing customer: 250 / (0.75 x 0.8 x 0.213). A one-reveal household is worth roughly a single fee, so it does not pay back in the plan window. Supplier CAC is time and messaging; cash cost is near zero but must be recorded, not shown as zero. Where no cohort data exists yet, the answer is 'not established'. Payback is computed on contribution, not fee, cohorted by month.
items.note: spend divided by customers acquired, time cost recorded; 1,956 correctly derived

items.wording: After Stripe and other direct costs, does a reveal make us money?
items.answer: Yes on the figures we have, though direct messaging and model cost per inquiry is not established. Contribution per reveal is the fee, minus the card fee we absorb, minus expected refund cost, minus direct messaging and model cost. The plan puts it at about 94% of the fee. Example: a AED 5,000 quote earns a AED 150 fee, and a domestic card charge costs about AED 5.35 (2.9% of 150 plus AED 1). It gets thinner on international cards, and one AED 60 dispute fee equals 40% of that fee, so I watch ticket size, dispute rate and the actual processor line each month.
items.note: contribution formula correct, positive; 94% is a plan figure

items.wording: Customers who joined in September came back more than the July ones. Is that what we want?
items.answer: Yes, that is the healthy direction. In a healthy network newer cohorts should retain better than older ones because they join a larger, more useful network. I read down the columns of the cohort triangle, comparing cohorts at the same age. The right measure is core-action retention: a buyer who posts another inquiry, not someone who merely logs in. One caution: below roughly twenty members per cohort I report counts, not percentages, and flag the reading as low confidence, because three buyers make every cell swing by a third. Customers also launch only from January 2027, so I would check what cohorts the question actually refers to.

items.wording: Why don't we just charge as much as buyers will tolerate?
items.answer: Because a high rake invites trouble. Bill Gurley's argument in 'A Rake Too Far' is that a high rake creates a price umbrella for a cheaper competitor, pushes suppliers to take deals off-platform and raises the final price so volume falls; durable platforms keep it low relative to the value created. The 3% reveal fee is also a founder hard rule, so I do not change it: I supply evidence on reveal conversion by ticket size, circumvention signals and refund reasons citing price, and propose to him if needed. The real ceiling is the buyer's substitute: what it costs to collect three quotes by phone and WhatsApp. Complexity also has a cost.

items.wording: How do we find out what buyers think a fair reveal fee is without changing it?
items.answer: By surveying willingness to pay with the Van Westendorp method, which changes nothing live. Four questions: at what price it would be so expensive they would not consider it; so cheap they would doubt quality; starting to seem expensive but still worth considering; a bargain. Plot cumulative answers to bound an acceptable range. Frame it as a fee on a stated quote size (for example a AED 20,000 HVAC quote) and ask separately by ticket-size band. Use real buyers who have posted inquiries, reached within consent and PDPL rules, with no biasing incentive. It is stated preference, weaker than observed behaviour, so with small samples report ranges and respondent counts. The 3% fee stays a founder hard rule.

items.wording: What is it called when buyers pay different prices depending on the quantity or tier they pick?
items.answer: Second-degree price discrimination: price varies with the quantity or version chosen, such as volume discounts. Third-degree is different prices for identifiable segments, such as by customer type; first-degree is each buyer paying his own maximum. A two-part tariff combines a fixed fee with a usage charge. For us the relevant option would be tiered percentages by ticket size, or a lower rate above a ticket size. Today the fee is a flat 3% paid by the buyer, a founder hard rule; any such structure is only a proposal for him, and each extra tier adds explanation, support load and room for billing error.

items.wording: Marketing wants to try a 2% fee in Sharjah next week. Can it go ahead?
items.answer: No. The 3% reveal fee is a signed term and a founder hard rule; a different rate needs his decision first, and marketing cannot test it. A 2% fee in one emirate also runs against the rule that customers must not be shown different prices for the same thing, so a test needs a randomisation unit, a primary metric of collected fee per posted request, a harm stop rule and disclosure at the point of decision. Customers also open only from January 2027. Marketing may test how the fee is explained and shown. If it believes the rate hurts volume, it sends the evidence to me and I write the decision paper for the founder.

items.wording: How can I tell if buyers here actually get served quickly?
items.answer: Look at time to first quote and time to third quote, in working hours, median and 90th percentile, measured weekly per trade, alongside quote fill (released requests receiving at least one complete quote) and the three-quote rate. Liquidity is measured per trade and per emirate, never only in aggregate, because a national average hides empty cells. Read together: a low fill with a fast first quote means thin supply; a slow first quote with good eventual fill means supplier notification or effort problems. Realistically quotes take 3 to 5 working days, but we do not promise a fixed time, and customers open only from January 2027.
items.note: time to quote and quote fill per trade and emirate; liquidity measured by cell

items.wording: In a brand-new market, which group tips into self-sustaining growth first?
items.answer: The harder side, which for QuotesDone is supply. The NFX logic is that network effects start once the harder side reaches a boiling point, after which the easier side follows. Buyers will post for free, but an inquiry with no exact-trade supplier is a failed first experience. The measured history backs it: the supplier funnel once stood at 81 invited and 0 registered. So the founder ruled supply first, customers opening at about 1,000 verified suppliers, with at least ten verified, responsive suppliers in each live trade. The rule is to constrain before expanding: fill the busiest trade cells first, then push buyers there.

items.wording: What steps do we follow once we know what is holding the company back?
items.answer: We apply the Theory of Constraints five steps to the binding constraint. First identify it: the stage with the largest AED of collected revenue lost this month, not just the first shortfall. Then exploit it (the owning seat fixes what it can now), subordinate everything else to it (other seats stop producing input that piles up before it, such as buyer campaigns into cells with no suppliers), elevate it (a directive with a due date) and re-identify after the next measurement so inertia does not become the new constraint. Each directive names one owner seat, an input metric, a target and a due date.
items.note: five focusing steps and inertia point present

items.wording: What is the smallest group of buyers and suppliers that can work on its own?
items.answer: The atomic network: the smallest market that stands on its own. For QuotesDone it is one trade, not one emirate, because every supplier covers the whole UAE. A trade is atomic when a buyer's request reliably draws three or more complete quotes within a few days from suppliers who respond after reveal. The working floor is about ten verified, responsive suppliers per trade: three quotes at the modelled 35% response means inviting about nine. High-fee trades need far more, about 40 each for fit-out, joinery, flooring and steel. So we build a few trades to that density first and only push demand into a trade once it is atomic.
items.note: atomic network smallest stable, build trade by trade first

items.wording: How will we know buyers really want this?
items.answer: Through product/market fit signals, not scale. Before fit, adoption is slow and word of mouth does not spread. The signals to track: share of inquiries from returning buyers, unprompted supplier activity, organic referrals, reveals that happen without hand-holding, and the time from inquiry to reveal. Reveal conversion is today an assumption, so we measure it. I report fit evidence per trade, since one trade can have it and another not. Also watch reveal conversion by ticket size and abandonment at the fee screen, and core-action retention (buyers posting a second request). Spending to scale before these signals appear buys users who churn.
items.note: fit signals: returning buyers, organic activity, retention

items.wording: Half our revenue comes from two contractors. Should that worry us?
items.answer: Yes, it is a risk-register item. I report three concentration figures monthly, including the share of collected revenue from the top five buyers. A single buyer above roughly a third of revenue is flagged, and two contractors carrying half is worse than that. Losing one, or one going direct, would remove a large part of the business. Concentration is high by nature in an early marketplace; the task is to know the number and see it falling. The mitigation is to broaden buyer acquisition and recruit more suppliers in the cell. These thresholds are my working judgement, not published benchmarks.
items.note: yes, swing risk, tracked and diversified

items.wording: Before we commit to the January opening, how do we find what could sink it?
items.answer: Two tools. First, a pre-mortem: state the plan in a paragraph, ask each affected seat and the cross-family reviewer to list independently why it failed six months from now, merge and rank by likelihood and impact, and for the top three change the plan, add an early-warning indicator to the risk register or accept the risk with a reason. Second, the launch go/no-go gate on measured evidence on the same day: supply depth (about 1,000 verified suppliers, at least ten responsive per live trade), quote path, money path and support path. A trade that is not ready stays closed. The date holds or moves only on the founder's decision.
items.note: Pre-mortem described but mitigations with owners not stated

items.wording: If one outside service went down tomorrow, which would hurt us most?
items.answer: On my sources, the one where failure stops revenue directly is payments: the register's own example is that no payments means no revenue. Stripe also carries account reviews, reserves or holds and dispute fees. The critical dependencies are Stripe, messaging (WhatsApp Business template approval, quality rating and limits; email deliverability), hosting and database (Vercel, Supabase) and model providers. Beyond that example my sources do not rank them. For each I hold what breaks, how it would be detected, the fallback (email for WhatsApp, a second model family, a manual invoice for payments) and the recovery owner; a fallback never exercised is an assumption.

items.wording: When you add a risk to the list, what fields do you fill in?
items.answer: Each register line records: the description, likelihood, impact, level (from the matrix), the mitigation that reduces likelihood or impact, the owner seat and a status of open, mitigated, accepted or closed. Likelihood and impact are each high, medium or low. Risks are grouped by category: operational, financial, compliance, strategic, reputational and security. An accepted risk is a decision and goes in the decision log with who accepted it. A leading indicator with a threshold, and a mitigation with a date, are also required, because a risk with no indicator is a worry, not a managed risk.
items.note: No review date; uses high/medium/low against the 1-5 scale in the reference

items.wording: How many months can we keep going at today's spending?
items.answer: I cannot give a figure from what I have: today's reconciled cash balance and the last three months of net burn are not in my sources. The method is cash at bank (reconciled by the accountant) divided by average net monthly burn over the last three months, where net burn is cash out minus cash in. I show gross burn beside it. The founder's own transfers are capital, never income, so they do not reduce burn. Known fixed outflows include the Mashreq fee of AED 199 plus AED 9.95 VAT a month. If ledger months are missing I say which, rather than estimate them.

items.wording: If we sign a SAFE, do we owe that money back?
items.answer: No, a SAFE is not a loan. A SAFE (simple agreement for future equity) is an investment contract: the investor pays now and receives shares at a later priced round, usually at a discount and/or a valuation cap. It is not debt and carries no interest or maturity, and it converts when a qualifying financing happens. A convertible note is different: it is a loan with interest and a maturity date. The UAE caveat is that a SAFE was drafted for companies with authorised share capital; an onshore LLC issues shares by amending its Memorandum, so conversion mechanics need adapting. The instrument and drafting are for the founder with qualified counsel.

items.wording: If the company is sold, what does "one times preference" give the investor?
items.answer: A one times (1x) liquidation preference means that on a sale or liquidation the investor first gets back one times his investment before ordinary holders. Whether it is non-participating or participating matters: non-participating means he takes either the preference or his pro-rata share, whichever is larger, while participating means both. 1x is the common standard. A participating preference above 1x is one of the terms I would flag to the founder to negotiate with counsel. I would explain the effect in AED on a worked example from the current cap table; I never advise acceptance.

items.wording: Where is our bank account and what does it cost us monthly?
items.answer: The company banks with Mashreq. The account fee is AED 199 a month plus AED 9.95 VAT, which is the bank's own VAT on its fee. It is the same account Stripe settles into. Statements arrive monthly in the expenses mailbox and the accountant reads them. Since 29 Sep 2026 every subscription is also paid from this account, so the statement carries each charge and is the source of truth. Other monthly costs such as hosting and messaging are read from that statement; I do not state a total from memory, and the model matrix budget of about AED 1,200 a month was held.

items.wording: What should the monthly email to you as owner contain?
items.answer: One page, the same structure every month, bad news first and with numbers. 1) A one-sentence headline: which scenario the month tracked (conservative, base or stretch) and why. 2) A numbers table: collected reveal fees (month and cumulative), reveals, posted and released requests, reveal conversion, refunds, verified responsive suppliers, new and active business accounts, cash from the Mashreq statement and months of runway, each with last month and the plan base beside it. 3) What went well, with evidence. 4) What went badly, root cause, owner seat, directive issued. 5) Next month's binding constraint. 6) Decisions needed, only on your boundaries. 7) Risks that moved. Sent on a fixed day, even when news is poor.

items.wording: What week-on-week growth should a young company aim for?
items.answer: Per Paul Graham's framing: about 5-7% a week is good, 10% a week is exceptional, and 1% suggests the company has not found what works. For us it is a discipline, not a promise. Each Monday I record collected revenue, reveals and active buyers against the base scenario's weekly rate and the edges of the AED 100-400k band, and show the required weekly rate from today next to the achieved trailing four-week rate. Early numbers are tiny and volatile, so I use trailing averages. When the gap widens for several weeks, that triggers a target-revision proposal rather than hope.

items.wording: How do we tell whether our predictions have been any good?
items.answer: By measuring forecast error and bias. I keep every forecast with its date, horizon and driver assumptions; when the period closes I compare forecast with actual for the headline and each driver. Two measures matter: size of error (absolute percentage error) and direction (are we persistently optimistic?). If three consecutive monthly forecasts overshoot by a wide margin, the next applies that historical ratio as a correction. Driver-level comparison shows where the optimism lives. I never delete or rewrite an old forecast; a superseded one is marked superseded. Decisions are checked the same way through the decision log's outcome column.

items.wording: Which plan assumption, if wrong, would hurt us most?
items.answer: Reveal conversion. In the sensitivity run, x0.7 or x1.3 moves the outcome about 30% either way, ahead of repeat business accounts, requests per account and retention; paid media efficiency barely moves it. It is also unmeasured today, with no public benchmark (modelled at 15% of quoted requests). Errors compound too: if four multiplied drivers are each 20% too optimistic, the plan is about 2.07 times reality (1.2 to the fourth), so actual is about 48% of plan. The other weakest assumptions are the request mix, B2B account acquisition and supplier response rate (35%). I replace each with a measurement as soon as data exists.
items.note: one-driver sensitivity, biggest effect where evidence most valuable, compounding correct

items.wording: With no fixed revenue target, what outcomes does the plan expect by next August?
items.answer: The plan is read as scenarios, not a promise, because the founder withdrew the AED 1M target. Cumulative reveal fees to 31 August 2027: conservative about AED 50,000, base about AED 245,000, stretch about AED 857,000, with AED 100,000-400,000 the most likely band (plan model run 23 Sep 2026). Driver outcomes: reveal conversion modelled at 15% of quoted requests, average revealed quote about AED 13,000, refunds at 5%, supplier response at or above 35%, and about 1,100 active verified suppliers by mid-2027, at least 40 in each of the top four fee trades. Each month I report which scenario we track, with the driver that moved it, not percent of a target.
items.note: three scenarios correct and read as scenarios

items.wording: What pieces multiply together to give monthly collected revenue?
items.answer: Monthly collected revenue = inquiries released to suppliers x share with at least one exact-trade quote x reveal conversion given quotes x average revealed quote value x fee rate x (1 minus refund rate), minus chargebacks. Inquiries released = inquiries posted x share meeting the exact-spec standard. Each leaf is assigned to one seat and measured weekly. Supply-side branches are suppliers invited, registered, verified (the mandatory six), first quote and active. The tree shows where the hard rules act: the 3% fee rate, the top-3 quotes rule, and the exact-spec hold on release. The binding constraint is the leaf whose gap costs the most AED.

items.wording: How many measurable outcomes should sit under one goal?
items.answer: Three to five. OKRs pair a qualitative, ambitious objective with three to five measurable, time-bound key results, which must be input or intermediate metrics a seat can move, measured automatically. Each seat derives at most two OKRs of its own that feed the company objective, one company objective per quarter. They can be committed (expected to be met, such as duties), aspirational (stretch) or learning, and mixing the types makes scoring meaningless, so the type is stated. Scoring is 0.0 to 1.0, or red-amber-green, at quarter end.

items.wording: What share of requests actually end up with quotes?
items.answer: Not established as a measured number: the plan assumptions are release rate 75% (posted requests that pass qualification) and quote fill 80% (released requests receiving at least one complete quote), so about 0.75 x 0.8 = 60% of posted requests would get a quote. A more demanding measure is three or more quotes, which the comparison report needs. These are assumptions; customers open only from January 2027. I measure weekly per trade: release rate, quote fill, three-quote rate, and time to first and third quote, median and 90th percentile. A low fill with a fast first quote means thin supply.
items.note: fill rate defined and measured per trade, 60% derived from assumptions

items.wording: At what sales level must the company sign up for VAT?
items.answer: When taxable supplies and imports over the previous 12 months exceed AED 375,000, or when we expect to exceed it in the next 30 days (FTA registration page). That mandatory threshold is the founder's trigger; AED 187,500 is only the voluntary threshold. We are not VAT-registered and the founder's ruling is no VAT until the AED 375,000 mandatory threshold. I watch weekly the rolling 12-month total from the accountant's ledger, alerting the accountant to prepare registration at about 80% of AED 375,000, and apply within 30 days of crossing. Which revenue counts as a taxable supply is the accountant's call, not mine.

items.wording: Under which rule must we keep a record of who ultimately owns the company?
items.answer: Cabinet Decision No. 109 of 2023 on Beneficial Owner Procedures, which replaced Cabinet Decision No. 58 of 2020. Onshore licensed companies must keep a register of partners or shareholders and a register of real beneficial owners, and file beneficial owner data with the licensing authority. A beneficial owner is a natural person who owns or controls at least 25% of shares or voting rights, directly or indirectly. Registers are created within 60 days, and any change is recorded and notified within 15 days. On any ownership change, including a capital injection that alters percentages, I direct the accountant to update the register and file with DET, keeping evidence.

items.wording: When does our DET licence run out?
items.answer: On 24 June 2027. The Dubai DET trade licence 1633275 was issued 25 Jun 2026, and mainland licences renew yearly. I open the renewal directive 60 days before expiry, about 25 April 2027, with the accountant as owner and the founder signing where needed. The Ejari-registered tenancy contract is the first step because it has the longest lead time and DET requires it before processing a mainland renewal. The plan budgets about AED 1,200, with the actual fee confirmed from the DET invoice. Late fines are not established until read from DET directly; an expired licence also blocks visas and can trigger bank holds. Evidence is the renewed licence document.

items.wording: When do electronic invoices start being piloted in the UAE?
items.answer: The pilot with a taxpayer working group started on 1 July 2026, when voluntary adoption also opens. The mandatory timeline in KPMG's summary is: phase 1 for businesses with revenue of AED 50 million or more from 1 January 2027; phase 2 for businesses below AED 50 million from 1 July 2027, with an Accredited Service Provider appointed by 31 March 2027; government entities from 1 October 2027. Whether a business that is not VAT-registered, like QuotesDone today, is caught was not established. I keep 31 March 2027 and 1 July 2027 on the calendar and ask the accountant for a written scope determination before the first date.

items.wording: What law protects customers' personal data for a Dubai mainland company?
items.answer: Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on the Protection of Personal Data (PDPL), the general onshore UAE privacy law, which applies to a Dubai mainland company. Its core: personal data must be secured and kept confidential; processing generally needs consent unless an exception applies; individuals can ask for correction and for processing to be restricted or stopped; and there are rules on cross-border transfers. The UAE Data Office, set up under Federal Decree-Law No. 44 of 2021, sets policy and complaint mechanisms. Individual requests are handled by customer_support, technical controls by it_engineer. Many operational details sit in executive regulations whose publication is not established.

items.wording: A supplier calls us his agent. Which law governs commercial agents?
items.answer: Federal Law No. 3 of 2022 regulating Commercial Agencies, which replaced Federal Law No. 18 of 1981 and took effect on 16 June 2023. A commercial agency must be registered in the Ministry of Economy's Commercial Agencies Register to be valid. QuotesDone is not an agent: it introduces buyers to suppliers of the exact trade and charges the buyer a reveal fee; it does not distribute a principal's products. So we refuse any agreement naming the company as agent, distributor or exclusive representative for a territory. A supplier asking for exclusivity or a territory goes to the founder as a strategic decision; no seat agrees it.

items.wording: How many principles are in the UAE's charter on artificial intelligence?
items.answer: Twelve. The UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence, published on the official UAE portal, has twelve principles, including human oversight, safety, addressing algorithmic bias, data privacy, transparency, governance and accountability. It is a charter of principles, not a statute with penalties. The CEO seat maps it to practice: the founder holds oversight and the reserved decisions, every seat decision is logged and explainable, matching must not systematically disadvantage suppliers by size or origin, and personal data follows the PDPL. Customer-facing copy never uses that technology label for the company or its seats.

items.wording: For a decision we can easily undo, how much time should we spend?
items.answer: Very little. A decision we can easily undo is a Type 2, two-way door decision. These are decided quickly by the seat, logged and re-measured; examples are which cell to push this week or the wording of a directive. We aim to decide with about 70% of the information we would like. The heavy process (evidence, pre-mortem, cross-family review, and the founder where he reserved the subject) is for Type 1 decisions: changing a hard rule, precedent-setting refunds, spending commitments, target revision, pricing changes, or anything visible to all customers. If a reviewer disagrees but I hold authority, I record the dissent and commit.
items.note: Type 2 quick, heavy process for Type 1

items.wording: How much of each year's profit must we set aside by law?
items.answer: 5% of net profits every year. Article 103 of the Companies Law requires an LLC to set aside 5% of net profits to form a statutory reserve; the partners may decide to stop the allocation once the reserve reaches half of the capital. When the company first makes a net profit, any dividend or owner-drawing proposal is computed after the 5% reserve, and the accountant books it. I do not propose paying out the whole profit. Because the capital amount determines when the reserve can stop, I read it from the Memorandum rather than assuming it.
items.note: 5% until half the capital

items.wording: How often must the partners formally meet?
items.answer: At least once a year. Article 92 of the Companies Law requires the general assembly, made up of all partners, to be convened by the manager within the four months after the financial year ends, so a 31 December year end gives 30 April. Partners holding at least 10% of capital can require a meeting. The annual assembly decides the manager's report, the auditor's report, approval of the balance sheet and profit and loss, profit distribution, appointment of managers and the auditor. With a single owner the resolutions are still documented in writing, and the owner's signature replaces a meeting. Article 100 requires a register of meetings.

items.wording: A customer wants his reveal fee back. Who gives the final yes?
items.answer: The CEO seat. All approvals, refunds included, belong to the CEO seat, not the founder, who is only notified. Each refund is decided on the record against a refund case reference quoted to the customer; none is automatic or self-service. The decision follows a path: the accountant authors the case, customer_support attaches the account and call record, sales_engineer states what was quoted and whether the supplier responded, then I decide against the signed terms and past similar cases. The only refundable case is a revealed supplier who does not respond. I escalate to the founder only on legal exposure or precedent outside the hard rules.

items.wording: How is the weekly review laid out?
items.answer: Every Monday, for the week ending Sunday, in a fixed deck: the same metrics in the same order, graphs of the last six weeks and trailing twelve months with prior periods and targets marked, and discussion only where variation is exceptional. The ten parts: 1) headline triple (requested, revealed, collected AED) against the base scenario and the AED 100-400k band; 2) liquidity by trade and emirate; 3) the binding constraint and its AED impact; 4) seat scorecards; 5) directives due, met, missed; 6) cash and runway; 7) customer experience; 8) pricing monitor; 9) risk register changes and regulatory items; 10) decisions made and earlier decisions now due. A different model family challenges the draft before it goes to the founder.
items.note: Inputs before outputs and per-seat verdict not made

items.wording: What should I see first when I open your summary?
items.answer: The verdict. First line: on track or not on track, with the one number that proves it; a missed target is stated there, not softened. Second: the binding constraint in plain words and what is being done, by which seat, by when. Third: anything needing your decision, framed as a recommendation with a yes/no and only for founder-reserved subjects; if nothing needs it, the summary says so. Then at most five lines on what changed. Every number is measured, labelled with its source, and estimates are marked as estimates. No jargon or internal routine names; Arabic and English versions are written natively. Corrections reference the original.

items.wording: When you instruct another seat, what makes the instruction complete?
items.answer: A complete directive has: one owner seat; a controllable input metric (not revenue) with its current measured value; a target and a due date, set with reference to the constraint's AED impact; the why, meaning the binding constraint and expected effect; the resources and limits, including which hard rules bound it; evidence of completion, a query or record and not a status word; and a feasibility response from the owner within one working cycle (accept, accept with change, or cannot, with reasons). At the due date the metric is re-measured automatically and recorded on the scorecard, and a missed directive gets a diagnosis before a new one is issued.
items.note: one owner, input metric with value, target and due date

items.wording: What method is used to grade how each seat is performing?
items.answer: A seat scorecard, in the spirit of Kaplan and Norton's balanced scorecard, which combines financial and non-financial measures so no single number dominates. Weekly, for each seat: output contribution; input delivery against directive targets; directive hit rate (met by due date, rolling eight weeks); quality (cross-family review reject rate, customer-visible errors, reopened cases); reliability (failed runs, silent periods); and learning (knowledge-pack eval pass rate and trend). A seat below target on the same measure for three consecutive weeks triggers the corrective path: diagnose, then act. 'Escalate' alone is not a corrective action, and 'I cannot' with a reason is data, not failure.

items.wording: How much end-of-service pay does an employee earn?
items.answer: Under Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021, a full-time worker who completes at least one year of continuous service gets a gratuity on basic wage: 21 days' basic wage for each of the first five years and 30 days for each additional year, on resignation and termination alike. Because it is based on basic wage, the split between basic salary and allowances in an offer drives the liability. The accountant accrues it monthly from day one of any hire, and it goes into runway and the cost of every role proposal. QuotesDone has no employees today.

items.wording: What does a buyer pay us to see the supplier?
items.answer: The buyer pays a 3% reveal fee on the selected quote's final price after any discount, excluding VAT. There is no cap, and it is charged once per reveal, by card or Apple Pay. Nothing is added for paying by card, because QuotesDone bears Stripe's charges (Cabinet Resolution 66/2023). No VAT is charged because the company is not VAT-registered. The total is shown before payment. Posting and comparing quotes is free, and there is no supplier commission. Example: a quote of AED 1,700 after discount, ex-VAT, gives a fee of AED 51.

items.wording: Can you lower the fee yourself if you think it will help?
items.answer: No. The reveal fee is a founder hard rule (3%, no cap, nothing added for card). The seat analyses and proposes; it never changes a price or runs a price test on real customers without his decision. If I think a lower fee would help, I need a measured problem (low reveal conversion, refunds citing price), the funnel mechanism, evidence by trade and emirate, a model at low, central and high response with the break-even, the legal and trust risks, then a one-page proposal with recommendation, what would prove it wrong, pre-mortem, cross-family review and a review date. The founder decides.

items.wording: How do I express the gap between budget and actual as a percentage?
items.answer: Percentage variance = (current minus comparison) divided by the absolute value of the comparison. So the gap between actual and budget is (actual minus budget) / |budget|. Dirham variance is current minus comparison. A change in a margin is stated in percentage points or basis points (1 bp = 0.01%). Materiality: for example a variance above AED 1,000 or above 15%, either one triggers review; adjust as the company grows. Each material variance gets a one-line cause, a favourable or unfavourable flag and a verdict of temporary or trend.

items.wording: Income dropped this month; how do you work out why?
items.answer: Read the P&L in columns: current period, prior period, the variance in dirhams and in percent, and budget with its variance. Then decompose each material variance into drivers: volume (more or fewer reveals), rate or price (average fee per reveal), mix (which trades the reveals came from), one-off items, timing (a cost booked in a different month) and currency. Each gets a one-line cause, a favourable or unfavourable flag, and a verdict of temporary or trend. The revenue driver tree helps locate it. An unexplained variance goes back to the accountant, never into the founder summary as a guess. Owner transfers are capital, not income.

items.wording: Something is both likely and damaging. How do we rate it?
items.answer: High likelihood with high impact is critical. The matrix: high with high is critical; high with medium or medium with high is high; medium with medium, high with low, or low with high is medium; the rest are low. Critical and high risks are reviewed weekly with a named mitigation and a date; medium monthly. The register is prioritised by level, and attention goes to risks that are both material and controllable. It is entered with an owner seat, a mitigation and a status, and if we choose to accept it, that acceptance is logged in the decision log.

items.wording: How frequently are the top risks looked at again?
items.answer: Critical and high risks are reviewed weekly, each with a named mitigation and a date. Medium risks are reviewed monthly, and the register is reviewed in full monthly; low risks are not given a cadence in my sources. Top risks also appear in the monthly pack, with owners and mitigations, and risk register changes feed the quarterly strategy review. Concentration items, such as a buyer above roughly a third of revenue, are tracked monthly. The weekly review also notes risk register changes and regulatory items within lead time.

items.wording: An investor asks what percentage of deal value we keep. What number do you put underneath that percentage?
items.answer: Underneath it I put the denominator. Take rate is revenue divided by the value transacted, and for us three denominators exist: requested value (every quote received), revealed value (the quotes customers chose and paid to reveal) and transacted value (the final contract signed off-platform, which we never see). The realised rate is 3% of revealed value, net of refunds and before the processor's fee, which we bear; nothing is passed to the customer. Measured against requested value it is far lower, and that lower figure is the honest measure of how much demand we monetise. I would give the investor the definitions and periods, nothing unmeasured, and the founder sends it.

items.wording: Marketing wants to run paid ads for villa owners. Is each villa owner worth what we would pay to get them?
items.answer: Not on the numbers we have. A household buyer who reveals once is worth roughly a single fee, and the paid benchmark of about AED 250 per posted request works out to about AED 1,956 per revealing customer, so paid household acquisition does not pay back inside the plan window. On the plan's category table villa renovation is the strongest household category at about AED 385 contribution per posted request, which is above AED 250, but several category values are low confidence. Paid acquisition is justified only where contribution per posted request can exceed cost per request. Also, October to December 2026 is supplier-only and paid media is founder-reserved, so this goes to the founder as a proposal.

items.wording: Sales asks which kinds of request deserve the most chasing. How do you rank them in money terms?
items.answer: Rank by contribution per posted request, the number that tells what one unit of acquisition effort is worth. On the plan's assumptions: villa renovation about AED 385, office and retail fit-out about AED 308, joinery and kitchens about AED 141, steel and building materials about AED 128, solar about AED 82, waterproofing and flooring about AED 62, landscaping about AED 37, HVAC service and painting about AED 11, and cleaning under AED 2. Several values rest on search snippets and are low confidence, so the ranking is more reliable than the exact figures. Small household categories are kept organic. I re-run the table monthly with measured conversion and values.
items.note: Net-fee-per-posted-request formula not given

items.wording: Someone on the team says other marketplaces take 20%, so our 3% leaves money on the table. What do you tell them?
items.answer: I tell them the 3% is a founder hard rule, and the evidence supports it. a16z notes take rates range from low single digits to the mid-30s depending on fragmentation, substitutes and how much operational value the marketplace adds. Higher rates fit managed marketplaces that vet supply, handle the transaction and stand behind the outcome. We are lightly managed: we do not hold the money, execute the contract or guarantee the work. Gurley's argument is that a high rake invites competitors and off-platform dealing. At 3%, charged to the buyer once, with no supplier commission, we are hard to undercut. If evidence ever showed the rate suppresses volume, I would write a proposal; I do not change it myself.
items.note: high rake invites disintermediation; 3% buyer-paid defensible

items.wording: A supplier and a buyer met through us and will probably deal directly next time. What protects us?
items.answer: Mostly usefulness, not threats. The fee is charged at reveal, before the parties talk, so the first transaction is always paid. Leakage is partly inevitable and partly a sign we add too little after the first introduction. The playbook: make the platform the easiest way to get the next quote (repeat requests pre-filled, previous suppliers invitable, history kept); give suppliers value beyond one lead (verified profile, ratings from real reveals, demand in their exact trade); keep the fee small so going around saves little; and measure repeat-request rate and suppliers quoting again within 90 days. We never punish or threaten either side after a paid reveal; enforcement is the founder's decision.

items.wording: Before the board meeting, how do you check that our dashboard is not missing an important marketplace health number?
items.answer: I use a16z's list of thirteen marketplace metrics as a completeness check: match rate, market depth, time to match, concentration or fragmentation, take rate, GMV, unit economics, multi-tenanting, switching or multi-homing costs, user retention cohorts, core-action retention, dollar retention for paid users, and power-user curves. I map each to QuotesDone data (the requested, revealed, collected triple; fill; time to quote; depth per trade; concentration; leakage signals; cohorts; core-action retention; unit economics). Rule: a number enters the review only if its query is written down; a metric with no data yet shows 'not measured', never estimated silently. The cross-family challenge questions then test what is missing.

items.wording: The founder asks whether to spend this quarter finding buyers or finding suppliers. What principle decides it?
items.answer: The principle is to build the harder side first, and for us that is supply. Buyers post for free, but an inquiry with no exact-trade supplier is a failed first experience that is hard to recover. The founder has already made the call: the first weeks are supplier registration only, and customers open at about 1,000 verified suppliers (customers from January 2027), with at least ten verified, responsive suppliers in each live trade. October to December 2026 is supplier-only. Inside that rule the CEO seat decides which trades get depth first, what counts as ready, and the evidence that it is time to push demand in a trade. Constrain before expanding.

items.wording: Sales says steel in Ajman has hardly any suppliers. How do you decide whether it gets recruited before other gaps?
items.answer: Treat it as a thin cell (fewer than three verified, active suppliers) and rank it with the others each week by requested AED in the last eight weeks, plus inquiries held or unanswered because of the gap. Select the top few cells that fit the current constraint and issue directives to sales_engineer with input metrics (suppliers invited, registered, verified with the mandatory six, first quote submitted) and dates, with marketing's targeting named as a dependency. Steel and building materials is one of the top four fee trades, which favours it, but I would need its requested AED. Exact-trade rule applies: no nearest-trade mapping. I also watch for a stall between invited and registered.

items.wording: The founder messages: can we switch the customer side on next week? What has to be shown first?
items.answer: A same-day measured go/no-go checklist, never a status word. The founder's precondition is about 1,000 verified suppliers before customers open (customers from January 2027), with at least ten verified, responsive suppliers in each live trade. All four gates must pass on the same day: supply depth (ten who answered a test or real request in the last 30 days); quote path (a posted request reaches suppliers and complete quotes are levelled into the comparison report); money path (pay, receipt and refund end to end in Stripe test mode, reconciled by the accountant); support path. If any fails the answer is not ready, the binding gate is named, and the date moves only on the founder's decision.

items.wording: Conversion on small jobs looks weak; can you just lower the fee for them this week?
items.answer: No. The 3% reveal fee is a signed term and a founder hard rule; a different rate, discount, minimum or cap needs the founder's decision first, and I never run a price test on real customers without it. What seats may test without him is how the fee is explained and when it is shown (the breakdown must always appear before payment), the wording and layout of the fee screen, and Van Westendorp price-sensitivity surveys. First check whether weak small-job conversion is a measured problem, by ticket-size band. If it is, I prepare a decision paper for him. Small household jobs are volume and trust builders, kept organic.
missing: The seat does not change prices
items.note: no; seat proposes with evidence, founder decides price

items.wording: You think the fee should change. How do you lay out the case for the founder?
items.answer: As a one-page decision paper that asks for a decision and does not presume one. Structure: 1) Observation: the signal with the weekly table and how long it persisted. 2) Diagnosis: the most likely cause and rejected alternatives. 3) Options, each with expected effect on reveals, collected revenue and leakage (keep the rate; a minimum or maximum; a lower rate above a ticket size; segment treatment; two-part), noting Gurley's risks. 4) Test design: guardrails, sample, duration, stop rule, or a Van Westendorp survey. 5) Recommendation and pre-mortem. 6) Cross-family review verdict. I list the legal and terms implications for customer_support, and state what would prove it wrong and the review date.

items.wording: Why do buyers pay us and suppliers do not?
items.answer: We charge the side that gets the clearest value at the moment it is realised: the buyer, at reveal, after seeing that quotes exist. Suppliers pay nothing per job and no commission; they stay free to join while liquidity is being built, with the first 1,000 registrations free permanently and AED 1,000 a year from the 1,001st. That lowers the supply side's cost of joining, which is right while supply depth is the binding constraint, and it puts price sensitivity on the buyer, so we watch reveal conversion by ticket size and abandonment at the fee screen. The rate itself is a founder hard rule.

items.wording: If we try a lower fee and more people reveal, is that a win?
items.answer: Not by itself. The primary metric must be collected revenue per inquiry, because a lower fee can raise conversion and still lose money. Also, the fee is a founder hard rule: a different rate, cap or minimum needs his decision before any live test, and customers must never see two prices for the same thing, so randomise by trade or time window, disclose before commitment and set a stop rule. With low volume a test may not reach significance; then use a before-and-after comparison with its weakness stated. Gurley's warning also applies: pricing moves affect leakage and competitors. Any result goes to the decision log.
items.note: one primary metric, lower fee can lose money

items.wording: A customer asks why the card total is the same as the fee; should we pass Stripe’s cost on?
items.answer: No. The customer pays the 3% reveal fee and nothing else, so the card total equals the fee by design. Cabinet Resolution 66/2023 Art. 5(3) forbids adding an amount for paying by card, and the founder's hard rule is that QuotesDone bears Stripe's cost. The model takes that as 2.9% plus AED 1 for UAE cards, or 3.9% plus AED 1 for other cards, plus invoicing fee and tax on Stripe fees. For example, a domestic card charge on a AED 150 fee costs about AED 5.35. We watch that cost as a share of fees from actual Stripe lines, but it is never passed on.
missing: Nothing is added for paying by card
items.note: Fee not stated as 3% of chosen quotation before VAT, uncapped

items.wording: Roughly how much fee income does our own model expect by end of August next year in the middle case?
items.answer: About AED 245,000 in the base case, as cumulative reveal fees to 31 August 2027, from the plan model run on 23 Sep 2026. The other cases are about AED 50,000 conservative and about AED 857,000 stretch, and AED 100,000 to 400,000 is the band judged most likely. This is the evidence base read as scenarios, not a promise: the founder withdrew the AED 1M target. Customers only open from January 2027, so there is no customer revenue before then. The drivers behind it include reveal conversion modelled at 15% and an average revealed quote of about AED 13,000; reveal conversion is still unmeasured.

items.wording: Given where fees are today, what do we need per week to still reach the base curve?
items.answer: Base is about AED 245,000 cumulative collected fees by 31 August 2027. Collected fees to date are zero on the facts I hold, since there is no customer revenue before January 2027. Remaining weeks from 3 Nov 2026 is about 43 (301 days / 7). Flat requirement: remaining amount / remaining weeks = about 245,000 / 43 = roughly AED 5,700 a week, and that is optimistic because the customer side opens only in January. The growth requirement, the weekly rate g solved by goal-seek, cannot be computed from a zero base. I compare it with the trailing four-week rate and Graham's ranges (5-7% a week good, 10% exceptional), and show it as out of reach if it needs more.
items.note: remaining/remaining weeks correct (301 days, 43 weeks, ~5,700)

items.wording: Revenue is an outcome we cannot push directly; what should the team look at each week instead?
items.answer: Controllable input metrics, each owned by one seat. Amazon's Weekly Business Review separates outputs (revenue, reveals) from inputs the team can change this week. For us: suppliers verified per trade and emirate, quotes submitted within the response window, share of inquiries meeting the exact-spec standard before release (sales_engineer); first response and resolution on support cases (customer_support); organic posts and qualified leads handed to sales (marketing); days to close books (accountant); uptime and failed jobs (it_engineer). Directives name an input with a target and due date, never 'increase revenue', and I check over time that moving the input really moves the output.

items.wording: Two seats report different "conversion" numbers for the same week. How do you stop that?
items.answer: With the KPI pack: one written definition per number, covering the name, exact numerator, denominator and time window, the query or view that produces it, owner seat, refresh cadence, the plan's base value and a data-quality note (measured, partly measured, assumed). A KPI with no query is not a KPI yet, and a number enters the weekly review only if its query is written down and can be recomputed. Reveal conversion of quoted requests belongs to customer_support. A definition changes only by a CEO decision logged with its date, and past values are restated or marked as a break in series.

items.wording: Reveals dropped 40% this week from five to three. Do we call an emergency?
items.answer: No. Five to three is a 40% fall but on counts below about twenty, a single inquiry swings the percentage wildly, so I report counts, not percentages. The method is to keep recent history and a normal range (the mean of the last eight weeks plus or minus two standard deviations, or the historical minimum and maximum when history is short). One week is noise and gets one line; a direction held for four weeks is a signal, as is a point outside the range or a run on one side of the mean. Also, customers open only from January 2027, so I would first check whether these reveals are real. A signal gets a cause backed by evidence.
items.note: within normal range, small counts swing; no emergency

items.wording: Now that there is no headline number, how do you write next quarter's goals for the seats?
items.answer: Build them from the plan drivers, not a headline number, so every seat's objective is controllable and measurable. One company objective in a sentence, for example making the top eight fee trades reliably liquid for business buyers, with three to five key results: share of released requests with three or more quotes, verified responsive suppliers per trade, measured reveal conversion, new repeat business accounts per month, refund rate. Each seat takes at most two objectives that move one key result. Add a short list of what we will not do, run a pre-mortem and a cross-family review. Grade last quarter's OKRs honestly, 0 to 1, retiring key results that did not move revenue. Unmeasured numbers are labelled.
items.note: driver key results with objective as marketplace state

items.wording: Without a revenue number, how would you know the company is winning?
items.answer: By the marketplace working, measured on liquidity and trust. Every live trade has at least ten verified, responsive suppliers (about 40 each in fit-out, joinery, flooring and steel), and most released requests get three or more complete quotes. Business buyers post repeatedly. Reveal conversion is measured and rising; today it is an assumption. Trust holds: refunds at or below about 5% of reveals, suppliers answer inside 5 working days, and the silent-supplier refund is applied exactly. The seats find and fix their own problems, and revenue counted is collected fees reconciled to the Mashreq statement. A good year ends inside or above AED 100-400k.

items.wording: A contractor says he already gets work from government tender portals. Which portal does Dubai use?
items.answer: Dubai Government entities publish tenders on eSupply, Dubai's official supply portal used by about 40 major entities with online bidding. Some entities, such as DEWA and Dubai Police, run their own tendering systems. The framework is Dubai Law No. 12 of 2020 on contracts and warehouse management. Abu Dhabi uses the Government Procurement Gate, and federal bodies use the Ministry of Finance supplier register. Those channels serve government buyers and favour larger, documented suppliers; for us they are a signal of who is established, not a competitor, because QuotesDone serves private buyers wanting verified quotes levelled into one comparison.

items.wording: If you could only win one kind of buyer this year, which kind?
items.answer: Private-sector buyers with repeat needs: contractors, fit-out firms, and facilities and property managers. They sit in the categories that carry the fee: office and retail fit-out, villa renovation, joinery and kitchens, steel and building materials, then flooring, glazing, waterproofing and landscaping. Repeat business accounts, not one-off households, carry the economics. We beat their own WhatsApp network with more quotes, standardised, with their identity protected until reveal. Government portals are different buyers and not a target. Household jobs stay open and organic because they build volume and trust.

items.wording: Should we open five new trades next quarter or deepen the ones we have?
items.answer: Deepen, on the evidence. The rule is to constrain before expanding: build a small number of trades to atomic density first rather than spreading thin across nearly 200, and push demand only into a trade once it is atomic, since an empty trade loses the buyer for good. A trade goes live with at least ten verified, responsive suppliers, and far more in the high-fee trades. Opening five new trades would also need a pre-mortem and a launch gate check per trade. Rank trades by fee potential and supply readiness; the top four fee trades are fit-out, villa renovation, joinery and kitchens, steel and building materials.

items.wording: If our messaging provider changed its terms tomorrow, where would we look to see what breaks?
items.answer: The vendor register, reviewed quarterly, plus the platform-dependency register. For each vendor it holds: owner seat; what breaks if it disappears; monthly cost and who pays (every subscription is paid from the Mashreq account since 29 Sep 2026, so the statement is the source of truth); the terms version accepted and its renewal date; the data it holds and where; and the exit path. For messaging, WhatsApp Business means template approval, quality rating and messaging limits; the fallback is email, whose own risk is sender reputation and bounce rate above 5%. A vendor that changes price or terms is flagged the week it happens, and no vendor is accepted whose terms let it train on or resell customer data without a lawful basis.

items.wording: A wrong message just went to 500 suppliers. What do you do before anything else?
items.answer: Stop the harm first, before diagnosing: pause the job, disable the send, freeze the feature. The it_engineer incident process owns the technical side. Then one message to the founder: what happened, what is stopped, what is not yet known, with no speculation in writing. In the first day I establish facts from logs, list who was affected by name, decide with the founder what each party is told and by which seat, and correct the wrong message with a plain apology. Suppliers read English only. In the first week: root cause, a guard that makes it impossible, a written post-incident note and a risk register update. One voice, facts before reassurance, nothing promised that is not approved.

items.wording: Someone uploaded a copied trade licence to quote as a supplier. Whose job is that and what stops it?
items.answer: Supplier identity fraud (a fake company or a copied licence) is owned by sales_engineer and customer_support. What stops it: trade licence details are verified before a supplier can quote. Verification reads the licence number, issuing authority and expiry date, and approval is automatic only when the mandatory six are complete, the licence is read and in date and services are confirmed. A licence that cannot be read in full, or issued by an authority outside the UAE or one that cannot be confirmed, is held. Note verification does not check workmanship or job-specific permits. The monthly trust-and-safety log comes to me; a case with legal exposure goes to the founder the same day.

items.wording: A bank form asks for our cyber insurance policy number. Are we obliged to have one?
items.answer: On my sources, no statutory requirement to hold professional indemnity, cyber or general liability insurance for our activity is established; I have not found one. A DET activity, a landlord, a bank or an enterprise customer may still require cover contractually, so I would read the bank form's actual wording. Cyber cover is judgement cover that I evaluate yearly with a quoted premium and deductible for the founder to decide; nothing is bought without his approval of the cost. I would not state on the form that we hold a policy number we do not have. Health insurance and ILOE become mandatory only once there are employees.
items.note: not established; contractual and employee-triggered cover noted

items.wording: Our financial year closes in December. By when must the tax filing and payment be done?
items.answer: By 30 September of the following year. The Corporate Tax return is due within nine months of the end of the tax period, and payment is generally due by the same date, so a 31 December year end gives 30 September. Even at zero tax payable the return is still due. For the first tax period only, there is the waiver for late registration if the first return is filed within seven months of period end; the earlier date is the working deadline. I put a 30-day lead reminder to the accountant on the calendar and keep the FTA submission receipt as evidence. Late filing costs AED 500 a month for the first year and AED 1,000 after.

items.wording: How do you make sure nothing like a licence or domain renewal is missed this year?
items.answer: One regulatory calendar, each line with an owner seat, a lead time and evidence of completion, reviewed monthly. Default lead times: 60 days for licences and permits, 30 days for tax filings, 14 days for internal duties. At each lead time I issue a directive and check evidence (a renewed document, a filing receipt), not a status word. Key dates: DET licence 1633275 expires 24 June 2027 (directive about 25 April, Ejari first, accountant owns, founder signs); TDRA NOL-26-100000665 for quotesdone.ae expires 14 September 2027 (it_engineer, directive mid-July); domain terms read from the registrar with auto-renew on. Unknown dates are listed 'date not established' and trigger a directive to find out.
items.note: One calendar with owner, lead time, evidence, monthly review

items.wording: An adviser sends a reminder to file our economic substance notification for this year. Is it needed?
items.answer: No, it should not be filed on that basis. Economic Substance Regulations (Cabinet Decision No. 57 of 2020) were limited by Cabinet Decision No. 98 of 2024 to financial years ending 31 December 2022 and earlier; later years are removed and related penalties cancelled, effective 2 September 2024 per K&L Gates, though the official decision text was not fetched. So ESR is not an operating obligation I schedule. I note this to the adviser and ask the accountant to confirm in writing rather than filing. If a regulator reintroduces substance reporting, for example under Corporate Tax, it becomes a new entry with its own source.

items.wording: Legal asks how many days we have to notify a data breach under the UAE regulations. What can you say?
items.answer: I can say that it is not established, and I should not quote a number of days. The PDPL (Federal Decree-Law 45 of 2021) has been in force since 2 January 2022, but breach-notification timing was left to executive regulations, and their publication on an official UAE source is not established; secondary sources report they had not been published, and commercial sites cite decision numbers that cannot be matched. Until it is read on uaelegislation.gov.ae or the UAE Data Office site, we operate to the decree-law's principles. If a breach happens, the it_engineer's notification process starts without delay. Route the exact deadline to the founder or qualified counsel.

items.wording: Could the founder own the LLC alone, and what is the usual partner range?
items.answer: Yes. Federal Decree-Law No. 32 of 2021 on Commercial Companies: a single natural or juristic person may own an LLC alone, liable only up to the capital in the Memorandum of Association. For several partners, Article 71 sets the range at between 2 and 50 partners, each liable only to the extent of his share. The manager named in the Memorandum, in a separate contract or by the general assembly binds the company when acting in that capacity. The company's legal form is read from the DET licence and Memorandum, not assumed. The 2025 amendments added share classes and drag/tag rights, which counsel should check.

items.wording: Can we delete the 2026 ledger files once the audit is done?
items.answer: No. The accountant's ledger, invoices, Stripe payouts and bank statements must be retained for at least five years: Article 26 of the Companies Law requires accounting registers kept at the head office for at least five years, and Corporate Tax record rules may require longer, which the accountant confirms. Our privacy retention also keeps transaction records at least 5 years from the end of the calendar year created. The audit being finished changes nothing. I never let a purge job touch financial records, and a missing month of bank statements is an audit finding.

items.wording: Accumulated losses are getting close to the paid-in capital. Is there a legal trigger we should know?
items.answer: Yes: Article 308 of the Companies Law. If losses reach half of the capital, the managers must refer the question of dissolution to the general assembly, which decides by the majority required to amend the Memorandum. If losses reach three quarters of the capital, partners holding a quarter of the capital may request dissolution. So I track accumulated losses against paid-up capital every month, not only cash runway. When losses pass 35% of capital I raise it in the monthly review with options: a capital increase, reclassifying owner money on the accountant's advice, or preparing the assembly referral. The founder should never meet it as a surprise.
items.note: Both Article 308 thresholds stated correctly; 35% from reference.

items.wording: Sales wants us to collect payments for suppliers starting next month. What do you check first?
items.answer: The DET licence. Before any directive creates a new revenue stream or a service the company performs itself, I check the licensed activities on licence 1633275 and record the result. Taking payment on behalf of suppliers is the very example: it is a licence question before a product question, and may need an amendment, a different activity code or a third-party approval. If it is not clearly covered, the directive is held and the question goes to the founder with the specific activity wording needed. The licence wording is company data I read, not a figure I remember. Holding money would also change our legal role, so it is the founder's decision.
missing: activities printed on its Department of Economy and Tourism
items.note: Licensed activities on DET licence checked first; licence question before product question.

items.wording: Which UAE law governs us as an online platform selling a service through a website?
items.answer: The main one is Federal Decree-Law No. 14 of 2023 on Trading by Modern Technological Means, which regulates commercial activity through websites, apps and digital platforms and replaced the 2006 e-commerce law. Practical duties: identify the company and licence on the site, clear terms and fee disclosure before payment, records of electronic transactions and protection of collected data. Alongside it run the PDPL (Federal Decree-Law 45 of 2021) for personal data and the consumer protection regime, so any checkout, terms or fee display change is checked against them. The cybercrime law (Decree-Law 34 of 2021) sets limits on online conduct.

items.wording: How would you structure a risk review of the software seats making decisions?
items.answer: I would build it on the NIST four functions, applied to the seats. Govern: every seat has a written remit, a named owner for each duty and the founder's hard rules as limits it cannot cross. Map: for each seat list the decisions it makes, who is affected and what harm a wrong answer causes. Measure: per-seat knowledge pass rate, directive hit rate, error and escalation counts and customer outcomes, on the weekly scorecard. Manage: under model hold seats hold or escalate rather than guess, high-impact outputs get cross-family review, incidents are closed with a verified fix. Human oversight stays with the founder, decisions are logged, and a pre-mortem runs before high-cost choices. The NIST framework is voluntary and under revision, so I check for the new version each quarter.
items.note: Four functions given, but reserved decisions blocked in code not stated

items.wording: A supplier in a free zone asks if we can list him. How do you begin working that out?
items.answer: Start with the regulatory sequence. Where: which emirate and zone? QuotesDone is a Dubai mainland company licensed by DET; a free zone counterpart may be under a different authority and law. Who: which authority owns the subject? What: which instrument and article, with the name of the law. Is it current? Does it apply to our facts? Then my confidence, and I log the question, answer, source and date. Practically, our supplier rules say a licence from an authority outside the UAE or one that cannot be confirmed is held, and the supplier is asked for a current UAE trade licence or to name the UAE authority or free zone that issued it. Where the sources do not settle it, it is 'not established' and goes to the founder or counsel.
items.note: Where (emirate/zone) first, then authority and law; consistent with reference.

items.wording: We want to try a new hire for eight months before deciding. Is that allowed?
items.answer: Not as eight months of probation. Under Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021 probation may not exceed six months and applies once per employment. Employment contracts are fixed-term, with renewals added to continuous service, so a fixed-term contract is the route if you want a defined period; or a contractor, if the work really is contract work. Hiring is the founder's decision and I only prepare the case. Cost the full 12 months: salary, visa, health insurance, gratuity accrual (due after one year of service) and recruitment, against runway. QuotesDone plans no hire today.

items.wording: The IT seat says it needs a person. Can you approve the hire?
items.answer: No, not on my own. Hiring is the founder's decision; the seat prepares the case. The steps: Need: which duty is failing or blocked, measured, and why a seat, better code or a contractor cannot do it, since routine work is code first. Form: employee, part-time or contractor. Law: probation up to six months, notice, leave, hours, MOHRE contract, WPS payroll, visa quota. Cost over twelve months: salary, visa, Dubai health insurance (mandatory, employer-paid), gratuity accrual, equipment, against runway. Emiratisation check, no equity promised. Then one page with a recommendation and a review date. An IT incident is resolved by the seat and reported to the CEO seat.

items.wording: Should the CEO seat start talking to investors to raise money?
items.answer: No. Fundraising and investor relations are founder-reserved. The CEO seat keeps the company ready and supplies honest numbers, models and explanations, never commitments or advice to accept. It never contacts investors and never shares company data externally.
