If the request was vague, we offer to help clarify the specification with all suppliers, and we quote no typical market percentages.

items.wording: A supplier with a gmail address and a price far below everyone keeps asking the buyer to WhatsApp him directly. Should we worry?
items.answer: Yes, worry, but without accusing anyone in writing. A free email domain for a company, a price far below everyone, and pressure to move to WhatsApp before reveal are all listed warning signs. Moving off-platform before reveal is also a breach of the anti-circumvention rule (AED 10,000 per incident for sharing contact details, and the higher of AED 20,000 or 5x the fee for taking a customer off-platform). What support does: not pass the account on a conversation, check the licence and TRN on the official registers, hold the quotation and tell the supplier only that verification is in progress, send the evidence to the CEO seat the same day, and the CEO seat decides suspension. Tell the buyer to stay on the platform and never pay outside the payment page. A supplier not being VAT-registered is lawful and is not itself suspicious.
missing: Pressure to move off the platform
items.note: Free domain, low price, off-platform pressure, register checks

items.wording: A customer has started swearing at the chat and calling us thieves. Do we keep going, warn him or stop?
items.answer: We keep going. First separate frustration from abuse. Swearing and 'thieves' said in anger about a charge or a wait is frustration: de-escalate, never warn, and check the charge or record behind the accusation. If it is abuse (personal insults, slurs, threats), reply once, calmly: we want to resolve this and will continue if the conversation stays respectful, and carry on with the substance. Only if the abuse continues do we pause the chat, say the case stays open and will be answered by email, and send it to the CEO seat. Threats of violence or self-harm go to the CEO seat at once (999 police, 998 ambulance). Keep the conversation unaltered, never retaliate, and any account restriction is a CEO decision in writing. There is no handover to a human on the homepage chat.

items.wording: An electrical contractor says a bad review is killing his business and wants it gone today. How do we handle it?
items.answer: We cannot promise removal today. Acknowledge his concern without promising anything, then check the rating against the published rules: was it submitted by the buyer of that RFQ, about that job, within the allowed window, and does it contain personal data, abusive language or unrelated content? A rating that breaks the rules is removed or edited by the process owner, with a record of why. A negative rating within the rules stays, and we offer a factual, courteous public reply if the platform supports it. If he alleges it is false, for example the work was never awarded, check the records; if they support him, the CEO seat decides. Never contact the buyer to pressure a change, and never trade a rating change for payment. Give him a decision date.
items.note: Acknowledge without promising removal, check against rules, only rule-breaking removed.

items.wording: Three emails from the same supplier about the same RFQ landed overnight, one is an out-of-office. What do we do with them?
items.answer: Triage by intent and owner, not by count. Detect that all three belong to the same case (same sender, same RFQ) and merge them into one case rather than opening duplicates. The out-of-office is an auto-reply and is not answered as if a person wrote it. Read the other two for what they ask: a question about quotation content, specification or commercial terms goes to the sales engineer through a handoff, since supplier questions arrive via support. Our reply is in English, keeps the case reference in the subject, and states the next step and when. Prioritise by impact and urgency, such as an RFQ deadline, not by tone.
items.note: Classify, merge into one case, do not answer out-of-office.

items.wording: A technician sent a voice note and short broken English about a delivery. How should our reply be written?
items.answer: Reply in the language the technician wrote in if we can produce it accurately; otherwise use simple English: short sentences, no idioms, no abbreviations, with Arabic added where appropriate. Never mock, correct or comment on his language, and do not guess a language from his name. For a voice note, acknowledge it and ask for the key point in text if we cannot understand it reliably. Write numbers, dates and amounts in digits and repeat them exactly, for example 'AED 1,250' or 'Monday 5 October', and ask him to confirm the key figure back. Anything with money or legal effect (fees, refunds, deadlines) is stated in English or Arabic, with a short translation if helpful and a note that the English or Arabic text governs. If he is a supplier's employee rather than the account holder, confirm who is authorised before discussing the account.
items.note: Own language if accurate, else simple English plus Arabic, voice note handling.

items.wording: The buyer asks if accepting the supplier's offer by clicking in the portal counts as much as a wet signature.
items.answer: Yes in principle, but I would not call them equal and I would not stop there. Decree-Law 46/2021 gives electronic documents and signatures legal effect; an electronic document does not lose validity or evidential value because it is electronic. The law has levels, and a qualified electronic signature carries the strongest evidential weight. Which transactions it excludes is not established, so I would not say any particular deed can be signed online. More important: revealing a supplier is not accepting the quotation. The contract for the work is made directly between buyer and supplier, usually by an LPO or signed agreement, and QuotesDone is not a party. The quotation is valid 30 days under our Terms. Specific enforceability questions go to the CEO seat.
items.note: TDRA licensing of trust service providers not mentioned

items.wording: Someone on WhatsApp just said "refund me now". Walk through what you look at before you answer.
items.answer: Before answering I look at seven things. 1) Which payment: date, amount, reveal and card last four digits, never full card data. 2) Whether a bank dispute is already open; if so, stop, the chargeback playbook applies and no parallel refund. 3) Whether an automatic rule has fired: reveal date, 5 working days counted with holidays, chaser at day 3; if the supplier stayed silent the refund is automatic, so confirm the issue date. 4) Which scenario it matches: duplicate or failed reveal, wrong supplier details, commercial disagreement, change of mind. 5) What can be said now, and that the CEO seat decides anything needing approval, with a date. 6) Timing: 5 to 10 business days, possible reversal, bank reference within 7 business days. 7) Record and hand off to the accountant and CEO seat in the same hour. I also check earlier reports from this person. The reply always has an answer and a date.
missing: Is a bank dispute already open
Never ask for full card data

items.wording: Our supplier invitations started landing in spam at Gmail. What would a senior check on our sending setup?
items.answer: First verify the sending domain's authentication before anything else: SPF, DKIM and DMARC records all passing and aligned with the visible From domain, valid forward and reverse DNS, and TLS. Then check the spam rate in Google Postmaster Tools (under 0.3%, advised under 0.1%), and that DMARC aggregate reports show only our own senders. Check hard bounces are suppressed at once and never retried. Check the unsubscribe: RFC 8058 one-click headers must be covered by the DKIM signature, and our endpoint was measured returning HTTP 400 on 125 of 146 calls, which loses real opt-outs and raises complaints. Gmail's bulk rules apply from about 5,000 messages a day. If bounces or complaints spike, treat it as an incident: stop the batch, read the Resend events, fix the cause, then resume. Never send from an unverified domain or a bought list.

items.wording: A supplier says he clicked unsubscribe twice and still gets our campaign emails. What has gone wrong and what do we do?
items.answer: Most likely our unsubscribe endpoint is failing. The 30 Sep 2026 senior-hire audit measured it returning HTTP 400 on 125 of 146 calls, so his opt-outs were probably lost. Support owns this function. Actions: suppress his address immediately in the sending path, not in a nightly job, and record the opt-out with time, address, channel and scope in the consent record; apologise once and confirm he will get no more campaign mail. Fix the endpoint so it accepts the one-click POST and a plain GET from the footer link and answers 200. Service messages he is owed may continue; marketing may not. Read the error log weekly and classify every non-200. Gmail expects opt-outs honoured within 2 days.
items.note: One-click POST, lost opt-outs, immediate suppression, service vs marketing; 125 of 146 correct.

items.wording: The dashboard says the FAQ deflected 300 contacts this month. Is that good news?
items.answer: Not by itself. Deflection is not success, because naive dashboards count a person who gave up as deflected. We count a self-service success only when the person did not contact us about the same issue within 7 days and did not abandon the journey, meaning the RFQ was still submitted or the payment still completed. So 300 is good news only if that check holds. Check it, then re-measure the contact rate per 100 active users, not raw counts. First contact resolution is likewise measured by the absence of repeat contact on the same topic, linked across channels. Never hide the contact route to push self-service.

items.wording: A contractor just emailed us a set of PDFs for a tender. Before anyone counts anything, what should be checked on each sheet?
items.answer: Read the drawing set as a set before counting. On each sheet check the title block: project, drawing number, discipline, scale, revision letter or number and its date, and status (for tender, for construction, for approval). Quote only against a named revision and list the drawing numbers and revisions priced, otherwise the quote cannot be levelled when drawings change. Then read the legend and general notes, plans, sections and elevations together, then details and schedules, which often carry the quantities. Check that disciplines agree and list each conflict as a written clarification.

items.wording: One wall on the plan has no length written and the sheet is marked NTS. Can I just measure it with a ruler?
items.answer: No. Where a note says do not scale, never scale a dimension; ask. A sheet marked NTS is not to scale, and a wall with no written length is missing information. Missing information on a drawing is a question to the customer, never an assumption in the price. Send a written clarification, and hold or flag the affected line until it is answered.

items.wording: The client wants to send us his Revit model and some JPG photos of sketches. What will the platform accept?
items.answer: Customers attach drawings as PDF, CAD (DWG/DXF, converted to a PDF sheet before it is read) or an image (JPG, PNG, HEIC, TIFF). Uploads accept JPG, PNG, PDF, DWG and DXF, up to about 1 GB. The JPG sketches are fine, with the customer's details covered. A Revit model is not among the accepted formats, so ask him to export DWG/DXF or PDF sheets from it.

items.wording: The ceiling height on the interiors sheet does not match the duct routing on the mechanical layout. Which should the supplier quote against?
items.answer: Neither, by choice. When architectural drawings disagree with MEP drawings, do not price either one. List each conflict (drawing numbers, revisions, what differs) and send it to the customer as a written clarification. Until it is answered, the affected lines are held, or priced with the assumption stated on the line and flagged. A supplier that silently prices the cheaper discipline has changed the scope.
missing: written clarification rather than choosing one
items.note: Neither by choice; list conflicts and send written clarification.

items.wording: The spec for the pumps says 'achieve 5 bar at the top floor' and names no brand. What kind of spec is that and what does it mean for quotes?
items.answer: That is a performance specification: it states a result to achieve and leaves the product to the supplier, as opposed to a prescriptive one that names a product, grade or method. It must be quoted with the product the supplier proposes and the evidence it meets the performance. So quotes will come with different models, and each must state the exact model, with datasheet and certificates, and cannot be ranked on brand alone. Compare on that evidence; a missing spec the trade checklist requires holds the line. If the supplier cannot meet it exactly, any alternative goes through the customer yes/no loop.
missing: leaving the product to the supplier
items.note: Performance spec; supplier chooses product, check evidence.

items.wording: The written spec calls for 20 mm porcelain but the floor plan legend says 10 mm. The client asks which we should price.
items.answer: I cannot choose for him, and I would not pick the cheaper reading. When the specification and drawings conflict, the contract's order of precedence decides, and there is no universal UAE rule that drawings beat specifications or the reverse. Many QuotesDone requests have no contract yet, so ask the customer in writing which governs (20 mm or 10 mm porcelain) and hold the affected lines until answered. Send the same clarification to every supplier so none gains information the others lack.
items.note: Order of precedence decides; ask in writing, never cheaper reading.

items.wording: I opened a 300-page spec book and I'm lost. How is it normally laid out?
items.answer: Specifications are usually organised by work section, using CSI MasterFormat divisions or the UK NBS structure, and are either prescriptive (a named product, grade or method) or performance-based (a result such as a fire rating or U-value). Read each section for named products and whether 'or approved equal' is allowed; standards cited (BS EN, ISO, GSO, UAE.S); test certificates and approvals required; submittals (datasheets, samples, shop drawings); warranties; and workmanship clauses. The specification says what quality is required; the drawings say where and how much.

items.wording: A consultant's BOQ preamble names the rules the quantities follow. Which rule books would you expect to see here in the Emirates?
items.answer: Three method-of-measurement rule books are common: POMI (Principles of Measurement International, RICS, 1979), still found on older and Gulf projects; NRM2 (RICS New Rules of Measurement 2) for building works; and CESMM4 (ICE Civil Engineering Standard Method of Measurement, fourth edition) for civil and infrastructure works. The preamble should name the one used. The sources do not say which method a UAE authority requires; that is set by the contract.

items.wording: Which version of the RICS detailed measurement rules is current and since when?
items.answer: NRM2, the RICS New Rules of Measurement 2: Detailed measurement for building works, second edition, published in October 2021 and effective from 1 December 2021. It gives the rules for measuring and describing building works in a bill of quantities, including preliminaries, contractor-designed works and risks.
items.note: NRM2 second edition, effective 1 December 2021.

items.wording: Our steel fixer wants 5% extra on the tonnage for offcuts. Do we bump up the BOQ number?
items.answer: No. Quantities are measured net as fixed in position, and waste, laps, cutting and offcuts are allowed for in the rate, not added to the quantity. Reinforcement is taken in tonnes from the bar bending schedule. If the fixer adds 5 percent to the tonnage, his total is no longer comparable: ask him to restate the quantity net and move the allowance into his rate.

items.wording: The road and drainage package comes with its own bill. What rules is that bill likely measured under?
items.answer: Most likely CESMM4, the ICE Civil Engineering Standard Method of Measurement, fourth edition, which is used for civil and infrastructure works. Confirm in the bill's preamble, which should name the method, because the contract sets it and the sources do not say which a UAE authority requires. Under these methods quantities are measured net, with waste in the rate.

items.wording: What unit should rebar appear in on a bill?
items.answer: In tonnes, by bar type and diameter, taken from the bar bending schedule where issued. Rebar priced per piece cannot be levelled against a measured bill, so ask the supplier to restate in tonnes. Waste and laps belong in the rate, not the quantity.
items.note: Tonnes by bar type and diameter from bar bending schedule.

items.wording: How do we quantify shuttering for the slabs and columns?
items.answer: Formwork is measured in m2 of contact area, by type: sides of foundations, soffits for slabs, and columns. It is measured net, and each line states its type. Leaving formwork out is a common error that makes quotes incomparable with a measured bill, so check every quote includes it or ask for it to be priced.
missing: formwork in m2 of contact area
items.note: m2 of contact area by type.

items.wording: One ready-mix supplier sent a price for 40 loads instead of cubic metres. Can I put it next to the others?
items.answer: Not as it stands. Concrete is measured in m3 by grade (for example C40), and a price per truck or per load cannot be levelled against a measured bill. Ask the supplier in writing to restate in m3 by grade and name the standard (BS EN 206). Send the same clarification to every supplier with the same gap. The number of m3 in a load is not established in my sources, so I will not convert it myself.
missing: concrete priced per truck rather than per m3
items.note: Not comparable; restate per m3 by grade.

items.wording: The mason priced block walls per piece. What unit should a take-off use?
items.answer: Square metres (m2), by block thickness and type (hollow, solid, thermal), measured net as fixed in position, not per piece. Waste and breakage belong in the rate, not the quantity. Ask the mason to restate his price per m2 so it can be levelled.
missing: blockwork in m2 by block thickness
items.note: m2 by block thickness.

items.wording: What should a painting line in the take-off say, apart from the area?
items.answer: A painting line is measured in m2 of surface and must state the full system: primer, number of coats and the product, plus the substrate. Every finishes line also carries its finish reference from the finishes schedule. A paint quote without the system or grade is held, not assumed.
missing: paint in m2 of surface stating the full system
items.note: m2 of surface with full system stated.

items.wording: The ceramic contractor's quantity is 10% higher than our measured area. Is that acceptable?
items.answer: Not as a quantity. Tile and stone waste (breakage, cutting) belongs in the rate, and a supplier who adds 10 percent to the quantity has changed the quantity, not the rate. Under the methods of measurement quantities are net as fixed in position. Ask him to restate the area net and move the allowance into the rate; otherwise his total is no longer comparable. Tiles are measured in m2 by tile size, grade and adhesive.

items.wording: How does the electrical bill quantify the wiring runs?
items.answer: By length, number and capacity. Cables are measured in linear metres by size, cores and type (for example 4C x 16 mm2 XLPE/SWA); containment (conduit, trunking, tray) in metres by size; wiring points (lighting, socket, data) by number; distribution boards, isolators and fittings by number from the schedule. Testing and commissioning, authority inspections (DEWA or the relevant distribution company for power) and as-built drawings are separate lines.
missing: cables in linear metres by size
items.note: Cables in linear metres by size, cores and type.

items.wording: The MEP contractor sent one number for electrical, plumbing and HVAC together. Is that usable for comparison?
items.answer: No. A quote that prices 'complete MEP' as one lump sum cannot be levelled; ask for the breakdown by system. Electrical, plumbing and HVAC are separate trades, so a mixed request is split into one request per trade, never mapped to a nearest trade. Each system needs its measured lines (cables in metres, pipes in metres, ductwork in m2 or kg, air-conditioning units by number with capacity) and testing, commissioning and authority inspections as separate lines.

items.wording: Two quotes both say '10 split units'. What details must be stated before comparing them?
items.answer: The count is the same but the item may not be. Each unit must be described by type (wall split, ducted, cassette, VRF indoor or outdoor, package), cooling capacity in kW or TR (1 TR = 3.517 kW), refrigerant, efficiency rating and power supply. Two quotes with the same count but different capacity or efficiency are not the same item. Beyond that, put both on the same basis: supply only or supply and install, piping beyond the standard length per metre, delivery point, VAT shown separately, validity, lead time, payment terms, and warranty period and coverage (compressor against general parts). Anything that cannot be normalised is listed beside the comparison, not ignored.

items.wording: A water heater importer asks which government body certifies his products for sale here. Who is it?
items.answer: MoIAT, the Ministry of Industry and Advanced Technology, which absorbed ESMA in 2020. It issues ECAS (Emirates Conformity Assessment Scheme) certificates, which are mandatory for regulated products before they are sold, and the voluntary Emirates Quality Mark (EQM). Whether water heaters fall under a technical regulation must be checked for the specific product in the MoIAT system.

items.wording: For sprinklers and alarms in a Dubai building, which rulebook does the fire authority use?
items.answer: The UAE Fire and Life Safety Code of Practice, 2018 edition. Dubai Civil Defence applies it to the design, approval, installation, testing and handover of fire and life safety systems, and approves fire products and fire contractors. A fire alarm, sprinkler or extinguisher line without Civil Defence approval evidence is held. If the site is in a free zone such as a Trakhees zone, confirm the location first before naming the approving authority.

items.wording: The warehouse fit-out is inside JAFZA. Do we go to Dubai Municipality for the permit?
items.answer: No. In Jebel Ali and the other zones of the Ports, Customs and Free Zone Corporation, building permits and EHS approvals come from Trakhees, not Dubai Municipality. Confirm that the warehouse is in a Trakhees zone, and ask for the exact location and free zone before naming any approval authority.

items.wording: A villa owner wants rooftop panels connected to the grid in Dubai. Who signs that off?
items.answer: In Dubai, DEWA approves rooftop solar connections under the Shams Dubai initiative, through DEWA-enrolled solar contractors and equipment on DEWA's approved list. So a solar quote must name the DEWA-enrolled contractor and the approved equipment, and the owner's connection is signed off by DEWA. Building permits are a separate matter and depend on the site, so confirm the location.

items.wording: The consultant wants lab test certificates for the blocks we supply in Dubai. Where are they usually issued?
items.answer: In Dubai, from the Dubai Central Laboratory, which Dubai Municipality runs. It tests construction materials and products and issues the conformity and product certificates used in Dubai approvals. Where the consultant requires a Dubai Central Laboratory certificate, a quote without it is held.

items.wording: A customer asks which permit authority applies to his project but only says 'Dubai'. What do you do?
items.answer: Ask for the location before naming any authority. I need the emirate, the community, and whether the site is in a free zone (for example a Trakhees zone, DMCC or a Dubai Development Authority area), because the permit authority differs. Never assume Dubai Municipality: no source gives a plot-to-authority lookup, and in Trakhees zones such as Jebel Ali the building permit and EHS approval come from Trakhees. Once I know the plot, I can name the authority for each approval, for example Civil Defence for fire systems and DEWA for connections.
missing: ask the location and the free zone
items.note: Ask location and free zone before naming authority.

items.wording: What grades does Dubai's green building rating have?
items.answer: Dubai's green building system is Al Sa'fat, run by Dubai Municipality. It has four levels: Bronze, Silver, Gold and Platinum. A level is achieved only by meeting all of its requirements, not by collecting points. The second edition was issued in January 2023. The requirements are grouped under ecology and planning, building vitality, and resource effectiveness for energy, water, and materials and waste.

items.wording: What is the lowest green rating a new Dubai building is allowed to achieve?
items.answer: Silver. Under Al Sa'fat, Dubai's green building system, new buildings in Dubai must reach at least the Silver level, so Bronze is not enough for a new building. A level is reached only by meeting all of its requirements. The second edition was issued in January 2023.

items.wording: A new private villa in Abu Dhabi: how many Pearls does it need at minimum?
items.answer: One Pearl. Under Estidama's Pearl Rating System in Abu Dhabi, 1 Pearl is the minimum for new buildings (all of them), and 2 Pearls for government-funded buildings. A new private villa is not government-funded, so the minimum is 1 Pearl.

items.wording: A supplier says his cable has the Emirates Quality Mark so it is the same as the mandatory certificate. True?
items.answer: Not true. ECAS (Emirates Conformity Assessment Scheme) certification is mandatory for regulated products, which cannot be imported, distributed or sold without it. EQM (Emirates Quality Mark) is voluntary and also assesses the manufacturer's quality system, typically requiring ISO 9001. Both are issued under MoIAT. For a cable, check which technical regulation applies, ask for the certificate, check it in the MoIAT system, and make sure it covers the exact model offered and is in date. A certificate for a different model or category is not accepted.

items.wording: A supplier left the tile thickness blank on two lines. Can those lines go to the customer?
items.answer: No. The exact-specs rule applies: a quote line is released only when it states every spec its trade requires, otherwise it is held and the missing specs are asked for. Tiles without size, grade and brand or approved equal are held, and thickness is a spec the flooring and tiling checklist requires. Never fill it with a guess, a typical value or a 'standard' grade. The hold message names the exact missing spec labels in one message. A line missing a required spec is never released by waiting.

items.wording: Who decides which specs a plumbing quote line must state?
items.answer: The trade's own spec checklist decides, not the seat's judgement. The spec_checklist entries of knowledge/packs/plumbing.json are loaded into public.trade_spec_checklist, and every one of the 213 trades in the taxonomy has a checklist. The seat applies the checklist of the exact trade and never fills a missing spec with a guess.

items.wording: How many trades in the taxonomy now carry a required-spec list?
items.answer: All of them: 213 trades. After the 28 Sep 2026 build, every one of the 213 trades in the taxonomy has a spec checklist (the spec_checklist entries of knowledge/packs/<trade>.json, loaded into public.trade_spec_checklist). The rule applies to services too.

items.wording: The paint quote doesn't say the grade. Can we assume the usual interior emulsion?
items.answer: No. The rule is exact specs or the quote is held. The seat never fills a missing spec with a guess, a typical value or a 'standard' grade, and never treats silence as acceptance. A paint line must state the full system (primer, number of coats, product) and the substrate, so the grade is asked for. The hold names the exact missing spec labels in one message to the supplier, in English.

items.wording: A cleaning company quoted just a monthly price. Is that enough since it's a service, not a product?
items.answer: No. The rule applies to services too. The specs of a service are its scope, deliverables, licences and qualifications held, service levels, duration and pricing basis. A cleaning quote with only a monthly price omits most of those, so it is held exactly like a goods line missing a grade, and the missing items are asked for in one message.

items.wording: A supplier quoted a brand of fire door. What documents should come with that price?
items.answer: The technical submittals: the manufacturer's datasheet for the exact fire door model offered; country of origin and manufacturer name; test reports or certificates against the standard named in the specification, from an accredited laboratory (ideally ISO/IEC 17025); the UAE approval that applies, that is Civil Defence approval for fire and life safety products; samples where the finish matters; shop drawings for fabricated or installed items; and the manufacturer's warranty terms. Check the model on the datasheet is the model priced, that certificates are in date, and that they cover the exact model and not just a family name. A missing submittal that the trade's checklist requires holds the line.

items.wording: The approval letter mentions the 'X-series' range, but the quote is for model X-450. Is that covered?
items.answer: No. A certificate counts only if it covers the exact model offered, not just a family name. Check that the model on the datasheet, the model on the certificate and the model priced are the same, and that the certificate is in date. An approval for the 'X-series' range does not establish cover for X-450 unless the certificate lists that model. Otherwise the line is held and the supplier is asked for a certificate covering X-450.
items.note: Certificate must cover exact model, not family name.

items.wording: A homeowner typed 'need tiling done, call me'. What is missing before we send it out?
items.answer: Almost everything. The inquiry needs: the exact trade and item (floor or wall tiling, tile size, grade, brand or approved equal, finish); quantities with units (m2); location down to emirate and community, plus access constraints; the required date; who supplies what (supply only, supply and install, labour only); drawings where the scope needs them; and warranty and payment expectations. A missing line specification is a hold, not a guess. List every missing item in one message in his inquiry language so there are not several rounds. Also, suppliers never see his phone or name, so 'call me' is not how it works; requests are made after sign-up and suppliers quote through the platform.

items.wording: What sits at the front of a bill before the measured items?
items.answer: The preamble comes first, followed by the preliminaries, and only then the measured work sections by trade. The preamble states the method of measurement, the specification and drawings the bill is based on, and the pricing rules. The preliminaries cover site set-up, supervision, insurances, temporary works and programme-dependent costs. After these come measured work by trade (item description, unit, quantity, rate, amount), provisional sums, prime cost sums, dayworks and a summary.
items.note: Preamble and preliminaries (site set-up, supervision) first.

items.wording: The bill has 'AED 50,000 for sanitary ware from the nominated supplier'. What is that?
items.answer: That is a prime cost (PC) sum. It is an amount the client names in the bill for specific goods or work from a nominated source, and the contractor adds profit and attendance on top. It is not the supplier's own price, so quotes are compared on the lines outside the PC sum. Do not confuse it with a provisional sum, which covers work that cannot yet be defined and is instructed later.
items.note: PC sum with profit and attendance made correctly

items.wording: A contractor reduced three of our quantities because he thinks they are over-measured. Is that allowed?
items.answer: Not silently. A supplier fills rates, not quantities. If a supplier changes a quantity it must say so as a qualification. Quantities are measured net as fixed in position under POMI, NRM2 or CESMM4, with waste, laps and cutting in the rate. So the contractor may raise his view that the three lines are over-measured, but only as a written qualification, and then his total is no longer comparable with the others. Ask him in writing to confirm the lines he changed and why, and level on the original quantities, or send the same clarification to all bidders so none gains information the others lack.

items.wording: How would you build up a rate for laying one square metre of block work?
items.answer: A unit rate is built as: materials (blocks and mortar per m2 plus breakage, at delivered cost) + labour (mason and helper hours per m2 at the all-in hourly cost, from an output rate) + plant and tools + a share of scaffold or access, then overhead and profit. The seat uses build-ups to test a quote, not to write it: check rate x quantity = amount and the sum, look for a rate that could not cover its own materials, and compare the same item across suppliers. Waste goes in the rate, not the quantity. Actual local rates are not established in my knowledge.
items.note: materials plus waste at delivered cost, labour, plant, overhead and profit all present

items.wording: On line 12 the quantity times the rate gives AED 4,500 but the amount column says 5,400. Do I just fix it?
items.answer: No, never fix it silently. Rate times quantity does not equal the amount, so the tender instructions or the contract decide which figure governs. If they are silent, ask the supplier to confirm in writing which figure it stands by. The same check is one of the quality flags that holds a quote: the supplier is sent the exact fix for the line, in English, and the quote is not shown to the customer as it stands. Do not guess which figure is the typo, even though 4,500 and 5,400 look like a transposition. Record the supplier's written reply.
items.note: never silently fix; written confirmation per tender rules

items.wording: Roughly how much of a typical UAE build cost is materials?
items.answer: About 60 percent of baseline construction cost, according to Turner & Townsend's UAE estimate, though it varies widely by trade. The rest of a typical trade quote is labour, plant and tools, preliminaries (reported about 12-15 percent on building projects), overhead, and profit (8-12 percent reported on mid-to-large projects). These are ranges, not rules.
items.note: around 60% stated with source

items.wording: Three quotes for the same fit-out look totally different in layout and totals. How do I make them comparable?
items.answer: Level them. Quote levelling turns quotes that look different into a like-for-like comparison. Steps: confirm every supplier priced the same request, revision and attachments; read exclusions, qualifications and assumptions before the price; build a matrix of scope items against suppliers marked included, excluded or unclear; send a written clarification for each gap with a deadline; where a gap remains, insert a plug with its source stated; only then rank. Normalise VAT (exclusive, shown separately), delivery point, units, brand, validity, lead time, payment terms and warranty, and mark each line compliant, deviation or not stated. Present the adjusted comparison and state every plug; a quote with five plugs carries more risk than one with none.

items.wording: Should the comparison table show prices including the 5% tax?
items.answer: No. Show every price VAT-exclusive, with VAT as a separate line, and record whether the supplier is VAT-registered (a TRN). A non-registered supplier does not charge VAT, which can make its price look 5 percent cheaper than a registered competitor, so the right comparison depends on whether the customer can recover input tax. A homeowner generally cannot, so for them the VAT-inclusive total is the real cost, which the VAT line makes visible. The UAE standard rate is 5 percent. The seat does not decide a party's VAT treatment; tax questions go to the accountant seat.

items.wording: What labels do you put on each line when checking a quote technically against the request?
items.answer: Each line is marked one of three labels. Compliant: the quote states the required spec and meets it. Deviation: it states a different spec, which is listed exactly. Not stated: the spec is missing, so the line is held and the supplier is asked. This is done before any price is compared, and a technically non-compliant quote is never ranked above a compliant one because it is cheaper.

items.wording: The cheapest quote uses a different cable type than requested. Can it still top the ranking?
items.answer: No. A quote that uses a different cable type than requested is marked as a deviation on that line, and a technically non-compliant quote is never ranked above a compliant one because it is cheaper. Its deviation is shown and the customer decides. Compliant quotes rank before cheaper non-compliant ones. The different cable is also an alternative the seat cannot accept for the customer: it goes through the spec-offer loop (supplier states the difference line by line, the customer answers yes or no), and an XLPE schedule cannot be swapped for PVC without re-checking capacity, voltage drop and fault withstand.

items.wording: A quote came in a quarter cheaper than everyone else. Should we tell the customer it's the best deal?
items.answer: No, not as the best deal. A quote far below the others is a risk signal before it is a saving. A quarter below the rest is beyond the roughly 15-20 percent below the median that industry guidance says to scrutinise (the working threshold belongs in decision_policy). Look for zero-priced lines, a rate that cannot cover labour, a different brand or grade, missing delivery or testing, a very short validity or a large advance. Do not recommend it and do not hide it: send a neutral written clarification and tell the customer it is under clarification. If the supplier confirms full scope, it stands and may be excellent value. A non-compliant quote is never ranked above a compliant one because it is cheaper.

items.wording: How do we choose between quotes when price is not the only thing that matters?
items.answer: Ask what matters to the customer: cheapest, fastest, a specific brand, longest warranty. The customer decides, so the seat does not impose weights. Score each quote on criteria such as total cost (price plus plugs, delivery, VAT treatment, payment terms), delivery, technical compliance, warranty, track record and commercial risk, apply the customer's stated priorities, show the calculation and document the weights. Level first so every quote is like for like; compliant quotes rank before cheaper non-compliant ones. Where the customer states nothing, show the levelled price comparison plus a short factual note on the non-price differences, then give a clear recommendation with reasons and what to clarify; the customer chooses.
missing: multiplies each score by a weight
items.note: weighted scoring of criteria, weights documented, customer decides

items.wording: Before a new supplier gets requests, what must we have confirmed about him?
items.answer: The mandatory six must be verified: (1) name, the legal trade name exactly as on the licence; (2) mobile, confirmed by OTP; (3) email, which is the account identity; (4) a valid, in-date trade licence checked at the issuing authority; (5) profile, with trades declared against the taxonomy, emirates served and service role; (6) the signed Supplier Agreement. The declared trades must fall within the licensed activities, and he must have confirmed the services he provides. Verification is within 3 working days of complete documents, a name mismatch is resolved before activation, and a supplier whose sanctions screening is pending or matched is never activated.
items.note: mandatory six including trade licence and signed terms

items.wording: None of the bidders can supply the exact chiller model. Can we just pick the closest one for the customer?
items.answer: No. When no bidder can offer the exact specification, an alternative is never accepted on the customer's behalf. The supplier states the alternative line by line (brand, grade, rating, dimensions, standard, approvals, warranty, lead time and price difference). Customer support then asks the customer one clear question: accept this alternative, yes or no. Yes makes it the accepted specification for that line; no means a polite apology to the supplier and the line stays unquoted by that supplier. An alternative that lacks a required UAE approval is not offered at all. The seat's part is technical: how it differs, and whether it meets the same standard and approvals.

items.wording: We sent the alternative to the customer three days ago and heard nothing. Can we proceed?
items.answer: No. Silence is not yes: the line stays held. The alternative becomes the accepted specification only when the customer explicitly answers yes. Customer support asks the customer; a reminder to the customer is for them to deliver, but the seat does not treat three days of silence as acceptance. The sources do not set a specific deadline for this question.

items.wording: The customer refused the substitute brand. What do we tell the supplier who offered it?
items.answer: The supplier receives a polite apology, and the line stays unquoted by that supplier. Tell him only that the customer declined the alternative. Do not share why in terms of any other supplier's price, identity or terms.

items.wording: The substitute sprinkler head has no Civil Defence approval but is cheaper. Should we put it to the customer?
items.answer: No. An alternative that lacks a required UAE approval, here Civil Defence approval for a fire product, is not offered at all. It never reaches the yes/no question to the customer, however much cheaper it is. A sprinkler line without Civil Defence approval evidence is held. Dubai Civil Defence applies the UAE Fire and Life Safety Code of Practice (2018 edition) and approves fire products and contractors. Only an alternative that holds the approval goes through the offer loop, where the supplier states the differences line by line and the customer answers accept yes or no.

items.wording: A supplier added a cheaper 'option B' brand at the bottom of his quote. How does it appear in the comparison?
items.answer: As a separate option, never folded into the base ranking. The base quote is compared like for like against the request; option B is shown as an alternate with its specific difference stated: brand, grade, rating, warranty, lead time and approvals status. The seat cannot accept it on the customer's behalf, because an alternate that departs from the customer's exact specification goes through the spec-offer loop, where the customer explicitly accepts it (it then becomes the accepted specification) or declines it. For regulated products an alternate must also hold the relevant UAE conformity certificate, otherwise it is not offered at all. Never blend the cheaper brand into the base price.

items.wording: To push the price down, can I let supplier A know that B came in 8% lower?
items.answer: No. Never disclose one supplier's price, identity or terms to another, not even 'a competitor is 8 percent cheaper'. The seat may say the offer is not yet competitive; it never says whose price is lower or by how much, and never invents a competing offer. Pressure tactics and false deadlines are not used. In any case, QuotesDone does not ask a supplier for a better price on the customer's behalf.

items.wording: Before we start pushing for discounts, what has to happen first?
items.answer: First level the quotes, so every figure is like for like, and know the customer's target, walk-away point and real alternative, which is the next-best levelled quote. Second, clarify before bargaining, because many apparent price gaps are scope gaps and are closed with written clarifications. Only then trade on what differs. The seat itself does not bargain on price for either party, offers no discounts of its own and never asks a supplier for a better price on a customer's behalf; it supplies evidence. Any request for a platform fee concession goes to the CEO seat.

items.wording: If talks with the preferred supplier fail, what is the customer's real fallback?
items.answer: The next-best levelled quote, not the headline cheapest one. An alternative that looks 30 percent cheaper can be weaker once scope and conditions are compared, so level the quotes first so the customer knows its true alternative. On QuotesDone every other quote is listed and the customer can choose any of them, and declining all quotes costs nothing. Reassess if a new quote or clarification arrives. The seat never misrepresents the customer's alternatives to a supplier and never reveals another supplier's price as leverage. After a reveal, price and terms are agreed directly between customer and supplier.

items.wording: The supplier won't move on price. What else can we ask for?
items.answer: Price is only one lever, and often the least productive. Besides price, the levers that create value for both sides are: scope split, delivery schedule, payment terms, retention (a lower percentage or a bond), warranty length and coverage, quantity for a better rate, validity, an approved equal at lower cost, installation responsibility, and after-sales service. The rule is trade, do not concede: each give is paired with a get. Note that QuotesDone itself never requests a discount from a supplier on a customer's behalf; any such talk after a reveal is directly between customer and supplier, and any agreed change goes in the revised quote.

items.wording: The main contractor wants to hold back part of each payment. How much is normal and when is it given back?
items.answer: Retention: a percentage withheld from each payment as security for completion and defects. In UAE practice practitioners describe 10 percent withheld from each interim payment, commonly capped at 5 percent of the contract sum per one guide, with half released at taking-over (substantial completion) and the rest after the defects notification period, often 12 months. A retention bond (bank guarantee) can replace cash retention on some contracts. Different sources give slightly different caps, so confirm the actual contract wording. Check that release conditions are objective, such as a handover date or defects period end, not 'to the owner's satisfaction'. It is typical for installation work in building projects, rare for simple supply orders.
items.note: 10% withheld, 5% cap, half at taking-over and half after DNP

items.wording: If a customer signs a one-year rate contract with a supplier, is the supplier promised a minimum order?
items.answer: Not as a rule. A framework or rate contract usually has fixed unit rates for a list of items, a term (commonly one year), call-off orders placed as needed, and usually no guaranteed volume. So the supplier is typically not promised a minimum order, unless the contract says so; the sources do not establish standard UAE framework terms, which are negotiated case by case. Check the minimum order values per call-off in the contract. On QuotesDone each call-off is a request with its own quote lines, respecting the reveal rule and the exact-spec rule.

items.wording: A supplier wants prices in the yearly agreement to rise with steel prices. What clause is reasonable?
items.answer: An escalation clause tied to a named index or a supplier notice, with a cap. That is what a senior checks in a framework: the pricing basis and any escalation clause, with the index named and a ceiling on the movement. For long lead-time items, state whether the price is fixed or subject to escalation, and state the clause. Which steel index to use is not established in my sources. Also fix the exact specs per line, so each call-off stays like for like.

items.wording: The customer needs a pool built. Can I send it to plumbers since pools involve pipes?
items.answer: No. A request is matched only to suppliers registered for its exact trade. A swimming pool goes to swimming_pools suppliers only, never to plumbing or civil works because the words look close. Matching is never decided by keyword overlap. If the pool trade has no supplier, the stalled-inquiry rescue widens only to uninvited suppliers in the same trade and emirate, and the gap feeds supply-gap detection.
items.note: no nearest mapping; swimming_pools suppliers only

items.wording: The request is for a trade we don't have in our list at all. What happens?
items.answer: The request is held, not matched, and never mapped to a nearest trade. New trades are welcome, but a trade is added to the taxonomy before anything is matched to it, and the new trade is proposed. The customer always receives the reason. If the request mixes trades, it is split into one request per trade. A request outside the platform's scope altogether (for example employment or loans, or food and beverage) is also held.
missing: a trade is added before anything is matched to it
items.note: held, trade added before matching, no nearest trade

items.wording: What are the non-negotiable rules our sales engineer must follow on every request?
items.answer: Exact trade match or none; exact specs or the quote is held; no word matching (meaning is reasoned, not keyword-scored); and UAE and GCC law only. Conduct rules: never share one supplier's price, name or terms with another, and never reveal a supplier's identity to a customer before a paid reveal; suppliers are written to in English on every channel, customers in their inquiry language; the reveal fee is 3 percent with no cap, no card fee and no VAT; never offer, request or promise a discount or an exception; never promise a turnaround, price, approval or refund. Route payment, refund and charge matters to the accountant seat, fee concessions to the CEO seat, close every loop, and do not contact the founder.

items.wording: A builder asks whether the ten-year structural liability survived the 2026 civil law change. What do you say?
items.answer: Yes, it survived. The new Civil Code, Federal Decree-Law No. 25 of 2025, effective 1 June 2026, keeps the decennial regime in Articles 821-824 (it was Articles 880-883 under the 1985 code). The contractor and engineer are jointly and strictly liable for ten years from delivery for collapse and defects threatening stability or safety; fault need not be proven, any waiver or limit is void, and the employer must claim within three years of discovering the defect. The new code excludes subcontractors from the statutory regime (Article 821(4)), so a main contractor pursues them by contract or fault. It concerns structural and safety defects, not ordinary finishes, and not a pure material supplier. This is general information, not legal advice; a dispute needs a licensed UAE lawyer.

items.wording: Our team uses a four-letter sales checklist for simple leads and a longer one for complex deals. Which is which, and when do we use each?
items.answer: BANT is the four-letter one: Budget, Authority, Need, Timeline. It is a fast screen and we use it on every inquiry, since most are single-trade jobs such as a villa AC replacement. MEDDIC (Metrics, Economic buyer, Decision criteria, Decision process, Identify pain, Champion) is the longer one, used only for large or multi-trade inquiries: who the economic buyer is, what the decision criteria are, how the decision is made (consultant approval, LPO, board sign-off) and whether there is an internal champion. What counts as 'large' is a threshold that lives in decision_policy, not in the text. Record which framework was applied and why, and do not interrogate a homeowner with enterprise questions.
items.note: BANT and MEDDIC correctly distinguished with use

items.wording: A villa owner insists the job must not cost more than a figure that seems low to me. How should I check his number before matching?
items.answer: Compare it with a documented market band before it shapes the match. In order of reliability: prices actually quoted on the platform for the same trade, emirate and specification in recent months; published market reports; supplier-provided indicative rates. Whole-building benchmarks (Turner & Townsend about US$1,926/m2 in Dubai; Knight Frank about AED 4,200/m2 for standard villas up to about AED 11,000/m2 high-end) must never judge a single trade package. If no trade-level band exists, say the band is not established. A budget far below the band is not a reason to reject: add a note to the customer ('quotes are likely to exceed this; proceed or adjust scope?'). Never share his budget with suppliers without his agreement.

items.wording: Someone on the phone wants a ballpark build cost per metre before he sends any drawings. How do you respond?
items.answer: I would not give a number. The seat answers a price question only from evidence and labels the evidence. First choice is the platform's own recent quotes for the same trade, specification, emirate and scale, stated as a range with the number of quotes and period. Second is a published benchmark with name and date, only when it fits the question's level; building-level figures never answer a trade question. If neither exists, say plainly that a reliable figure is not established and that the fastest way to a real number is to request quotes. Without drawings there is no scope to price. Never invent a number or present one supplier's quote as the market price; prices are exclusive of VAT.
items.note: evidence-only, labelled sources, never invent a number

items.wording: The client needs the steel frame on site in a month. Is that realistic, and how do lead times affect which quote wins?
items.answer: Probably not. Turner & Townsend's 2025 survey reports structural steel at 12-18 weeks in Dubai and 9-12 weeks in Abu Dhabi, against a one-month need. Lead time is compared as carefully as price. Record for each quote whether lead time runs from order, advance payment, approval of shop drawings or site readiness; ask whether the item is ex-stock in the UAE or made to order or imported; warn the customer early when the required date cannot be met. An unusually short lead time for a long-lead item is a point to clarify ('please confirm ex-stock availability and the model'), not a reason to prefer it. Lead-time performance against promise also feeds the supplier's score.
items.note: steel 12-18 weeks Dubai, lead time compared like price

items.wording: A supplier asks whether he will need new invoicing software soon in the UAE. What do you tell him?
items.answer: Probably yes, in time. The UAE is introducing mandatory Peppol-based e-invoicing through Accredited Service Providers, reported to the Federal Tax Authority. Per the summary I hold: pilot and voluntary phase from 1 July 2026; mandatory from 1 January 2027 for businesses with revenue of AED 50 million or more (ASP appointed by 30 October 2026); mandatory from 1 July 2027 for the remaining in-scope businesses (ASP by 31 March 2027). Most small platform suppliers fall in the July 2027 wave. Penalties described include AED 5,000 per month for failing to appoint an ASP. This is not tax advice, and whether it applies to his business goes to the accountant seat and the FTA. Dates are re-checked at each quarterly knowledge refresh.

items.wording: The fine print says "price excludes scaffolding" on one quote and "price assumes access from ground floor" on another. How do I treat each?
items.answer: They are different things. 'Price excludes scaffolding' is an exclusion: the item is simply not priced. 'Price assumes access from ground floor' is a qualification: the item stays in the price only if the assumption holds. Read exclusions and qualifications before the price, classify each by impact, and send a written clarification for every high-impact one, the same to every supplier with the same gap. Resolve by negotiation, by adding a plug (an estimated cost for the missing item, with its source stated), or by a written scope letter. Never let an unaddressed qualification pass into the order, and never name another supplier's price.
items.note: exclusion vs qualification correctly treated with plug and clarification

items.wording: I want to ask a bidder about some unclear lines on the phone. Is that fine?
items.answer: Not as the record. Every question to a supplier about its quote is written, specific, time-bound and recorded: it names the quote reference and revision, lists numbered questions tied to a line or clause, states the reply deadline, and asks for a revised quote if the price changes. A phone call may help you understand, but any answer that changes scope or price must be confirmed in the revised quote document, because undocumented verbal clarifications are a common cause of later disputes. Send the same clarification to every supplier with the same gap, and never disclose one supplier's price or identity to another.

items.wording: A bid has errors the system caught. Does the customer see it now, and how is the supplier told?
items.answer: No, the customer does not see it as it stands. A flagged quote is held. Every 15 minutes the quote quality duty sends the supplier the exact fixes, line by line, in English, once per distinct set of flags. The hold lasts 24 hours by policy; a quote corrected within the hold is released to the customer, and when the hold expires the duty acts on its rule and the customer is told. A line still missing a required spec is never released by waiting, and only the version the submission gate accepted is ever released. The fix message names the line and the exact correction and never says what a competitor quoted.

items.wording: The CEO wants to know if our comparisons are fast and complete enough. Which numbers do we report?
items.answer: The weekly comparison KPI duty measures three things: hours from inquiry to its comparison report (median and p90), the share of reports with three or more complete quotes, and how many quotes and reports carry exclusions. Three complete, comparable quotes is the practical minimum for a fair comparison; a report with fewer says so plainly. Customers launch from January 2027, so before then no inquiries flow and the KPI is null; that is reported as 'not measured', never as zero or as good.
items.note: median/p90, 3+ complete quotes and exclusions all stated

items.wording: A new supplier uploaded a licence scan. How do I know it is real and covers what he wants to quote?
items.answer: A scan is not proof. The licence is checked at the issuing authority, not only from an uploaded image: UAE licences are issued by each emirate's economic department or by free-zone authorities, and free-zone companies are verified with their free zone. Capture the licence number, legal name, legal form, issuing authority, status, expiry date and listed activities. If a registry cannot be reached, the item stays unverified and is never marked verified from the image alone. Then check coverage: his declared trades must fall within the licensed activities, decided by meaning, and the name on the licence must match the profile. A licence from an authority outside the UAE, or one that cannot be confirmed, is held.

items.wording: A trader of tiles wants to also offer laying tiles on our platform. What do we check?
items.answer: A valid licence is not enough: the declared trades must be within the activities listed on the licence. A company licensed for building materials trading can supply tiles but is not thereby licensed for installation or contracting work. For each declared trade and service role, find the licensed activity that covers it and record the pairing. Decide by meaning, citing the activity wording, not by keyword overlap. If none covers laying, the trade is not activated for matching and the supplier is told which activity is missing. Also check at the issuing authority, not only the scan, and that the name on the licence matches the profile.
missing: within the activities listed on its licence
items.note: declared trades within licence activities; trading licence does not cover installation

items.wording: Something feels off about a supplier who just registered. What would make you pause him?
items.answer: Any of these red flags would justify holding activation and asking questions (none alone proves wrongdoing): licence name differs from the profile, bank or invoice name; licence expired, cancelled or issued by an authority other than claimed; declared trades outside licensed activities; a free-mail address for a company claiming a large operation; a mobile number already linked to another supplier account (possible duplicate); documents that look edited or cannot be confirmed at the issuer; unwillingness to sign the terms; requests to communicate or be paid off-platform; certificates for a different model; unverifiable approval claims. Response: one polite message asking for the specific evidence, no accusation, record the flag. Duplicate or fraud suspicions go to the accountant seat; sanctions matches go to the accountant seat and the CEO.

items.wording: An investor asks whether we check suppliers against terrorist lists. Which UAE body keeps those lists?
items.answer: The Executive Office for Control and Non-Proliferation (EOCN) administers the UAE's targeted financial sanctions lists: the Local Terrorist List and the Countering Financing of Proliferation list. The legal screening, freezing and goAML obligations fall on regulated entities, and an ordinary B2B marketplace is not listed as one. QuotesDone screens counterparties anyway as a trust and risk control, and the accountant seat owns ongoing sanctions and UBO re-screening. At onboarding we collect the legal name, licence and owner or manager name accurately, never activate a supplier whose screening is pending or matched, and route any possible match to the accountant seat and the CEO without telling the supplier the reason.

items.wording: A supplier wants us to delete his mobile number from our records. Which UAE law applies?
items.answer: The Personal Data Protection Law, Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021. A supplier's contact person, mobile and email are personal data even in B2B, and data subjects have rights including deletion and objection. The request goes to customer support, which owns PDPL rights requests (also via management@quotesdone.com). Retention rules may limit what is deleted: supplier KYC is kept for the relationship plus 5 years under the tax-records rule. Whether the Executive Regulations have been issued could not be verified as of the 23 Sep 2026 check, and the seat does not decide the request.

items.wording: A supplier's licence runs out next week. What has he already received, and can he still get requests after it lapses?
items.answer: The licence expiry watch runs daily and asks for the renewed licence at 30, 14 and 7 days before expiry. With the licence running out next week he has already received the 30-day and 14-day asks, and the 7-day ask is due. After it lapses, no: an approved supplier does not stay matchable. He is paused, told why and what to send, and held out of matching until a renewal is uploaded and verified. Each ask is closed only when a replacement document arrives and is verified, never because a message was sent. A senior also checks the renewed licence carries the same legal name and still lists his matched activities.

items.wording: The customer sent an LPO after the supplier quoted. Do they now have a binding deal?
items.answer: Not automatically. A supplier's quotation is normally an offer and the buyer's LPO is the acceptance, but an acceptance must match the offer. An LPO that changes price, quantity, delivery date, payment terms or brand is a counter-offer the supplier must accept. So check the LPO against the accepted, levelled quote (reference, revision, lines, totals, VAT, delivery, payment, validity), confirm the quote was still within validity when accepted, and ensure the signatory has authority. Flag any mismatch to both parties before work starts. Electronic acceptance is valid under the UAE electronic transactions law when its reliability requirements are met.

items.wording: A customer wants to accept a quote from two months ago at the same price. Can he?
items.answer: Not as of right. A quotation is valid for 30 days from submission unless refreshed or withdrawn before reveal, so a quote from two months ago has expired. If a quote expired, ask the supplier to reconfirm or revise rather than treating the old price as binding, and do not assume a price will hold because the customer was slow. Material costs have been rising, and for long lead-time items check whether the price is fixed or subject to escalation. If the supplier reconfirms, record it as a revision.
items.note: only within validity, expired quote reconfirmed, rising costs and escalation

items.wording: A supplier asks whether a ministry job will tie up his cash for long. What is typical?
items.answer: Typically 45-60 days for federal government and Abu Dhabi government entities, and about 45-75 days for Dubai government and semi-government entities, according to one UAE practitioner source. So a federal ministry job would typically tie up cash for roughly 45-60 days. Under FIDIC 1999 Red Book the engineer certifies within 28 days and the employer pays within 56 days after the engineer received the statement, though 60-120 days is common in practice. These are reported observations, not legal limits; contractual terms govern.

items.wording: The main contractor's order says the supplier gets paid only once the client pays him. Is that normal and valid?
items.answer: It is common and not unlawful, so valid in that sense. A pay-when-paid clause makes the contractor pay the supplier only after he is paid by the employer, and pay-if-paid makes payment conditional on being paid at all. Per Kayrouz & Associates, the UAE does not prohibit these clauses, so suppliers lack protections available elsewhere and should negotiate independent payment deadlines. How UAE courts treat a particular clause was not established. The seat surfaces it as a commercial risk, explains it in plain words and never describes it as unlawful. It is also a reason a supplier may price a contractor's inquiry differently. For a specific dispute, route to customer support and recommend legal advice.

items.wording: A customer paid a supplier four months late. Can the supplier add interest?
items.answer: Possibly, depending on the contract. Under the Commercial Transactions Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 50 of 2022), as summarised by Nour Attorneys: Article 88 gives a creditor interest on a commercial debt from the maturity date unless the parties agreed otherwise; Article 89 lets parties agree a rate but the court may reduce an excessive one; Article 90 says where no rate was agreed the court sets it by market conditions, not exceeding 12 percent per year. Interest is simple by default, and the claim must be documented. I do not calculate a legal claim or threaten a customer with interest on the supplier's behalf; disputes go to support and the accountant seat. If the order itself states a late-payment rate, that is a term to surface before acceptance.

items.wording: A supplier wants post-dated cheques from a customer for security. What changed in the law?
items.answer: Federal Decree-Law No. 14 of 2020, effective 2 January 2022, changed the regime. A cheque bounced for insufficient funds is no longer automatically a crime; criminal liability remains for bad-faith acts such as stopping payment without legal cause or closing the account to defeat the cheque. Where the account holds part of the amount, the bank must pay the available balance and the holder can pursue the rest. Practitioners describe a dishonoured cheque as enforceable directly through the execution court. A supplier asking for post-dated cheques as security is a normal commercial term: show it in the comparison and make sure the customer understands a cheque is a payment commitment. The platform does not collect, hold or present cheques; refer enforcement to a licensed lawyer.

items.wording: An invoice from 2021 was never paid. Is it too late to claim?
items.answer: I cannot say it is too late; that is a legal determination, and the seat must not make it. The general rule: under Federal Decree-Law No. 50 of 2022, commercial obligations between merchants must generally be brought within five years from when the cause of action arose (Afridi & Angell). The old 1993 law allowed ten years, and there are transitional rules around 2 January 2023: where applying five years would already have extinguished a right before that date the old ten-year period applies, and where more than five years remained the remaining time is capped at five years. Which case a 2021 invoice falls into depends on facts I do not have. Give the general rule with its source and recommend a lawyer for any actual claim.

items.wording: The order has a delay penalty of 1% per day. Is the supplier stuck with it whatever the actual loss?
items.answer: No, not automatically. Liquidated damages are a pre-agreed sum, usually a rate per day with a cap, but under UAE law they are subject to judicial review: practitioners cite Civil Code Article 390 (1985 code) as giving courts power to vary the agreed amount if it is excessive or insufficient. So an LD clause is not a guaranteed figure, and the seat does not present it as an automatic entitlement or calculate penalties for either party. It is a material commercial term that must be visible in the request so suppliers price the risk, and the delivery date it attaches to should be realistic against lead time. A customer frustrated by delay goes to customer support's dispute process.

items.wording: Halfway through, the customer wants extra sockets. How is that priced and agreed?
items.answer: As a numbered variation. A variation is a change to the ordered scope. Write it with description, quantity, rate basis, price, time effect and VAT, agreed by both parties before the work is done. Rates for added quantities should come from the accepted quote's unit rates where the item is the same (sockets are measured as wiring points by number); new items are priced and, for meaningful sums, compared with a market band or another supplier. For small platform jobs there is often no engineer: customer and supplier agree directly. Unpriced verbal variations are the classic source of final-account disputes. The seat records variations in case memory.
items.note: variation defined, written and priced and agreed before work

items.wording: A supplier has not been paid for two invoices and wants to down tools. What can he do?
items.answer: This is background, not legal advice, and the seat never tells a supplier to stop work. Practitioner summaries describe: suspension of performance under the Civil Code's exception of non-performance (Article 247 of the 1985 code), requiring written notice, proportionality and good faith; under FIDIC 1999 Sub-Clause 16.1, suspension after 21 days' notice with time and cost entitlement; precautionary attachment of the debtor's assets, after which proceedings must be filed within eight days; and payment orders for undisputed documented debts. Document applications and certifications and issue formal non-payment notice first. The seat collects the documents, routes it into the platform dispute and accountant handoff, and tells him suspension carries legal risk and a licensed lawyer should advise.

items.wording: An importer quoted CIF Jebel Ali and another DDP site. What framework explains the difference?
items.answer: Incoterms 2020, published by the International Chamber of Commerce: 11 rules that define where risk passes and who pays carriage, insurance and customs. CIF is a sea-only rule: risk passes on board at the port of shipment and the seller insures. DDP puts the most on the seller: it delivers and clears import including duties, so a foreign seller may not handle UAE clearance well. To compare, bring both to one delivery basis by adding freight, insurance, UAE customs duty, port and clearance charges, inland transport and offloading, stating each assumption. Always name the place and the edition ('CIF Jebel Ali', 'DAP site Dubai Hills'). An Incoterm does not settle ownership transfer or payment.

items.wording: One supplier quotes ex-warehouse Sharjah and another delivered. How do I compare them?
items.answer: Put them on the same delivery basis before comparing totals. Convert the ex-warehouse Sharjah quote to delivered by adding transport to site and offloading, stating each assumption, or ask the supplier in writing to price delivery. Normalise the other fields too: VAT shown separately, scope, units, validity, lead time, payment terms and warranty. A difference that cannot be converted is listed beside the comparison, not silently ignored. Send the same clarification to every supplier with the same gap.
items.note: same delivery basis, add transport and offloading to ex-warehouse

items.wording: A customer is about to unlock a AED 200,000 quote. What will he pay on top, exactly?
items.answer: The reveal fee is 3 percent of the selected quote's final price after any discount, excluding VAT, so 3% x AED 200,000 = AED 6,000, assuming AED 200,000 is the final price before VAT. That is all he pays QuotesDone: no cap, no card surcharge (QuotesDone bears Stripe's charges), and no VAT on the fee because QuotesDone is not VAT-registered. The supplier's price itself is agreed and paid directly between customer and supplier, and QuotesDone holds no money for the job. Any VAT on the supplier's price is never part of the base. Payment is by card or Apple Pay through Stripe.
items.note: 3%, no cap, no card surcharge, no VAT; AED 6,000 is correct arithmetic

items.wording: I paid to unlock a contractor a week ago and he is ignoring my calls. Do I lose my money?
items.answer: Not necessarily. The one refundable case is when the revealed supplier does not respond. The clock runs from your payment without you doing anything: on day 3 (working) QuotesDone chases the supplier, copying you; on day 5 the case goes to QuotesDone's CEO for a final call; if the supplier still does not respond, everything you paid is refunded, with nothing deducted, and banks take 7-14 working days to show it. There is no self-service refund and every refund is decided by the CEO with a case reference. No refund applies if the supplier responded by any reasonable means (including WhatsApp or phone), if you already dealt with him off-platform, or you changed your mind. You can copy supplier@quotesdone.com when writing to him. I cannot promise the outcome; refund questions route to the accountant seat.
items.note: Supplier's liability (processor fee, AED 500, 12% interest) not stated

items.wording: A Sharjah contractor messages us on WhatsApp in Arabic about his quote. How do we reply, and what about customers?
items.answer: Reply to the contractor in English. Suppliers are always written to in English, on every channel (email, WhatsApp, portal, quote fixes, scorecards), even if the supplier wrote in Arabic. Customers are answered in the language they selected for the inquiry, English or Arabic, in proper Modern Standard Arabic, with technical terms kept in their standard English form. WhatsApp is customer support's channel, so I hand the message to customer support to deliver, and route any question about charges or refunds to the accountant seat.

items.wording: We invited 170 suppliers and only one quotes. How should this be reported and fixed?
items.answer: Report onboarding as stage conversion, not one count: invited (delivery verified in the outbox, not merely queued), registered, verified, activated, first quote, first quote chosen. Break every metric down by trade, emirate and source. Zero or low conversion must be checked against invitations actually delivered before concluding suppliers are uninterested, and a rising registration count with a flat first-quote rate means onboarding fills the database, not the marketplace. The fix depends on where the funnel breaks: one consolidated list of missing items for registrants who stalled, naming the exact missing item, then activation and a quick first suitable inquiry. External benchmarks are not established; compare against our own history. Report weekly to the CEO seat with the one constraint most limiting activated supply.

items.wording: A newly approved supplier has had no work for three weeks. Why does that matter and what do we do?
items.answer: It matters because a new supplier who waits weeks for work tends to disengage; activation is not the goal, quoting is. So check his trades, emirates and service role are set so matching can find him, watch for his first matching inquiry, and if none arrives within a set window tell him honestly about expected demand in his trade. Customers launch from January 2027 and October to December 2026 is supplier registration only, so if there is no live demand in his trade, say the platform is building supply ahead of launch. When the first inquiry comes, make sure he understands line-by-line quoting, exact specifications, VAT, validity and lead time, then give brief factual feedback and record time-to-first-quote.
missing: a supplier who never quotes adds nothing
items.note: activation not the goal; check trades/emirates; first inquiry handling

items.wording: The customer wants to know how reliable a supplier is on deliveries. Which measure would you use and how is it computed?
items.answer: OTIF, on-time in-full: deliveries on time and in full divided by total deliveries. A delivery is good only if it arrives within the agreed window or earlier and with the complete quantity and items ordered. About 95-99 percent is often considered excellent in general supply chains, not a construction benchmark. Fix and document the choices first: order-level or line-level, the tolerance window, which date counts (promised in the accepted quote, or a later date agreed in writing), and exclude customer-caused delays. Delivery results come from customer support's delivery confirmation; a delivery without a result is excluded, not counted as success. Use it only once the supplier has enough deliveries; the minimum lives in decision_policy.
missing: OTIF = deliveries on time and in full / total deliveries
items.note: OTIF formula correct

items.wording: Our best-rated electrician wants requests for plumbing too. Does his score help?
items.answer: No. The score ranks only suppliers who have already passed every hard gate: exact trade, emirate served, service role, verified, licence valid. It never lets a supplier bypass a gate.
