Matching is exact trade or none, with no nearest mapping, so an electrician gets plumbing requests only if plumbing is a declared trade in the taxonomy and his licence activities cover it; otherwise it is not activated and he is told which activity is missing. His score is only used for ranking within trades he is eligible for.

items.wording: New suppliers complain they never get a chance because old ones always rank higher. What is the fix?
items.answer: Build fairness into the score. A score that only rewards past wins is self-reinforcing. Safeguards: a neutral starting position plus a guaranteed share of eligible inquiries (an exploration share) for new or low-sample suppliers; scoring on rates per inquiry received, not totals; confidence adjustment so two perfect jobs do not outrank fifty very good ones; decay so old behaviour counts less; excluding events outside the supplier's control; and a right for the supplier to see its components and contest a data error. Also watch supply concentration per trade and emirate and recruit more supply where one supplier takes most matches. Percentages live in decision_policy.

items.wording: A supplier asks how he is doing compared with others in his trade. What does he get from us and when?
items.answer: Once a month each approved, reachable supplier receives last month's scorecard by email, in English, comparing his own figures with his trade: requests matched, quotes submitted, response time, share of quotes held for missing specs or quality fixes, reveals, outcomes reported by customers and ratings. It names no competitor and shows no competitor's price. A senior uses it to tell him which behaviour moves his matching score: respond within the window, decline with a reason instead of silence, state every required spec, keep the licence current. An address that is not sendable is recorded as not_sendable with the reason.

items.wording: The founder asks whether the marketplace is working for customers. Which single measure answers that?
items.answer: Fill rate (also called match rate): the share of buyer demand that finds suitable supply and transacts. Per inquiry the ladder is: matched to at least one eligible supplier; received at least one complete quote; received enough quotes to compare; customer chose or revealed; job delivered. Reporting by rung, by trade and emirate shows where it fails and who owns the fix. Customers launch from January 2027, so before then it is not measured.

items.wording: Requests for glazing in Fujairah keep getting no bidders. Whose job is it and what happens?
items.answer: It is the sales engineer's job to find the gap, and marketing's to run the recruitment. A supply gap is a trade-and-emirate segment where real demand cannot be served. Meanwhile the stalled-inquiry rescue widens invitations to uninvited suppliers in the exact trade and emirate and tells the customer honestly, and a request with nobody to invite is re-measured later. The sales engineer records the gap with evidence (affected inquiries, period, fill-rate rung) and hands marketing a structured recruitment brief. Do not infer a gap from a single inquiry; a minimum count lives in decision_policy. The sales engineer then onboards each recruited lead through the mandatory six, reports stage conversion by source, and the gap is closed only when the segment's fill rate recovers.

items.wording: How do I decide which categories need careful supplier development versus simple catalogue buying?
items.answer: Use the Kraljic matrix, which classifies purchase categories by profit impact and supply risk. Non-critical (low impact, abundant supply) needs an efficient process and catalogues. Leverage (high impact, abundant supply) uses competition, with fast levelling. Bottleneck (low impact, supply risk, for example some fire-safety or specialist glazing work in smaller emirates) needs supply-gap recruitment and closer relationships. Strategic (high impact and high risk) needs market monitoring and developed alternatives. Apply it to trade-and-emirate categories; the examples are illustrative and the real classification must come from platform data.

items.wording: We suspect customers find suppliers here and then deal with them directly next time. What is that called and why does it matter?
items.answer: It is called leakage, or disintermediation: buyers and suppliers use the marketplace for discovery and then complete the deal outside it. It matters because it stunts growth and suppresses monetisation, and it removes the customer's protections: the record of quote and acceptance, dispute handling and performance history. Signs include a supplier asking for a phone number in a quote note, quotes withdrawn right after a reveal, and repeat pairs that stop appearing. Never facilitate contact exchange outside the reveal rule, explain factually what they keep by staying, flag suspected circumvention to the accountant seat, and never accuse without evidence. The terms also bind: a business customer avoiding the fee owes it plus the higher of AED 5,000 or 3 times the fee; a supplier taking an introduced customer off-platform owes the higher of AED 20,000 or 5 times the fee, for 24 months.
items.note: leakage defined, stunts growth and monetisation

items.wording: The customer posted his job two days ago and still sees zero bids. What is happening behind the scenes?
items.answer: The stalled-inquiry rescue. A request with no quote 48 hours after matching is flagged no_quote_48h, and so is any open request with no live quote and zero reachable suppliers (found every 15 minutes). Every 30 minutes the rescue measures the pool of suppliers in the exact trade and emirate who were not yet invited, widens the invitation to them, and tells the customer honestly what is happening. It never widens to a nearest trade and never promises a number of quotes. A row with nobody to invite is re-measured later and feeds the supply-gap duty. It ends when a quote arrives or the request is closed. Realistically quotes take 3-5 working days, and no fixed time is promised.

items.wording: One of our installers is on another big job for two weeks. How does the platform treat him?
items.answer: A supplier can mark himself busy until a date. A busy supplier is not matched while busy, which protects his response rate and the customer's wait. Every 15 minutes the availability duty returns him to available on the day his busy date arrives (Dubai time), with nothing for him to do. He is treated as capacity information, not a penalty: a busy supplier is not counted as non-responsive. A long or repeated busy period is a reason to check whether the segment needs more supply.

items.wording: Who makes sure a request moves from intake to a hired supplier without waiting for instructions?
items.answer: The sales engineer seat. It owns the pipeline of every inquiry from intake to delivered job and chases anything stalled, rather than waiting for a CEO directive. Stages: new; qualified or held; matched; quotes received; comparison presented; customer decision; ordered; delivered; rated. Each stage has an expected dwell time in decision_policy, and anything past it is stalled and chased. Every chase and outcome goes to case memory, with a weekly report of counts per stage, stalled count and top stall reasons. Customer support delivers the messages.

items.wording: A company signed up last week but never asked for anything. Do we contact them, and how?
items.answer: Yes. The seat owns customers end to end, and customer support delivers the message. A customer with no request after 3 days gets a nudge; at 10 days a reasoned message is written for that specific case, not a template; and after 60 days with no request and no reveal there is a win-back nudge about their own trades. The messages go in the language the customer selected, one message per reason, with no generic campaign (that belongs to marketing), and every send is verified in the outbox, not assumed from a status column. Marketing messages go only with consent.

items.wording: A customer unlocked a supplier last month. Do we ever check how it went?
items.answer: Yes. The follow-up duty runs every 6 hours: on day 3 and day 14 after a reveal, the customer is asked whether they hired the supplier and how the supplier was. The answer is recorded as an outcome that feeds the supplier's score and the win/loss review. Customer support delivers the message, in the customer's language, once per reason.

items.wording: A customer has gone quiet for two months. Do we send him the newsletter?
items.answer: No. A customer with no request and no reveal for 60 days gets one win-back nudge about their own trades, never a generic campaign, which belongs to marketing. One message per reason, in his inquiry language, verified in the outbox. Marketing messages need consent, so I would not add him to a newsletter on the strength of silence.

items.wording: A customer says the contractor did half the job; the contractor says the customer changed the scope. Who rules?
items.answer: QuotesDone is not a party to the contract, and a dispute between customer and supplier is theirs to resolve. Internally, customer support collects both sides' statements and evidence by a due date, and the sales engineer's disputes duty reasons a finding from documents: customer_upheld, supplier_upheld, shared, or no_fault. That finding goes to the CEO seat, which decides; the sales engineer recommends and never decides a refund or charge itself. Work from documents: the quotation and revision, accepted scope and exclusions, LPO or written acceptance, delivery notes, dated photos, and platform messages. A scope change should have been a numbered variation agreed by both before the work; unpriced verbal variations are the classic source of final-account disputes.

items.wording: We lost five customers who chose not to reveal anyone. How do we find out why?
items.answer: Run a win/loss review for the outcome 'no decision'. Internal reason codes alone are unreliable, so ask the customers, in their own language, a short optional set: why this quote, what nearly changed their mind, and if none was chosen, why not. Prefer 'what' and 'why' questions. Code the reasons into a fixed taxonomy plus the quoted text and review patterns monthly by trade. The fill-rate ladder also shows at which rung they stopped, since a failure after quotes points to price, trust or customer readiness. Declining every quote costs nothing, so no pressure applies. Findings feed matching, the intake form, supplier coaching and the CEO seat.
missing: the buyer's own account is needed
items.note: Win/loss review using buyers' own account

items.wording: A supplier dispute looks like one we handled last month. Should the seat remember that?
items.answer: Yes. Before qualifying, matching, levelling, answering a price question or handling a spec-offer, the seat retrieves the most similar past cases by meaning (trade, specification, emirate, scale, customer type), reads their decisions and outcomes, cites the precedents it relied on, and says when none was found. Precedents inform but do not bind: a different specification or date can change the answer, and a case from before a rule change is marked as such. A past supplier's price is used only in aggregate, never revealed. After the outcome is known, write the case: subject, decision, rationale, evidence, outcome, whether final.
missing: decided as if it were the first
items.note: retrieve similar cases before deciding; precedents inform not bind

items.wording: The seat gave a customer a hedged answer and was corrected. What makes sure that does not happen again?
items.answer: The learning loop. Daily, a knowledge-gap sweep files every conversation where the seat hedged, was corrected, or had its reply rewritten as a knowledge gap and fills it with a sourced entry. Weekly, the quality review writes each lesson into seat_case_memory so the next similar case is decided with the precedent. Monthly, the self-review re-runs the qualification exam and opens a finding for every failed item. Before deciding, the seat retrieves similar past cases by meaning. A correction is data: the same mistake twice means the knowledge or rule lacks a home, and the fix is to give it one.

items.wording: Who should answer a supplier asking for his money back on a penalty?
items.answer: The accountant seat. Payment, refund, charge, non-response charge and billing questions route to the accountant seat, by a handoff that carries the evidence and the exact question, and the originator closes it after the reply is verified. Approvals, refunds included, are decided by the CEO seat. The sales engineer does not restate or vary the amount, and does not promise a refund. Customer-facing messages are delivered by customer support.

items.wording: One contractor gets requests every week and never answers. What do we do?
items.answer: First check the matching, then talk to him, rather than blame him. Measure his non-response as a rate over matched inquiries, separating 'declined with a reason' (acceptable and useful) from silence. Ignoring an invitation carries no penalty before a reveal; the non-response charge applies only when a revealed supplier does not respond and the customer is refunded. Make declining easy with a one-tap reason code, remind once before the window closes, and message him first with the facts, asking whether his trades, emirates or capacity should be updated. Repeated 'not our trade' declines mean matching or his profile is wrong, which we fix. A sharp score drop triggers a message explaining why and how to recover, not silent exclusion. Any charge, dispute or refund goes to the accountant seat.

items.wording: A new customer keeps seeing these three-letter abbreviations on quotes. How would you explain them?
items.answer: RFQ is a request for quotation. BOQ is a bill of quantities. LPO is a local purchase order, the buyer's purchase order to a local supplier. DLP (or DNP) is the defects liability or notification period after handover. IPC is an interim payment certificate. APG is an advance payment guarantee, a bank guarantee securing an advance. PDC is a post-dated cheque. TRN is a tax registration number. ECAS and EQM are the UAE product conformity certificate and quality mark. Exclusion, qualification and clarification are the quote small-print categories, and a plug is an estimated cost inserted for missing scope when levelling.
items.note: RFQ, BOQ, LPO correctly explained

items.wording: Which marketplace term describes how long a customer waits for usable suppliers?
items.answer: Time to match: the time from inquiry to a usable match. It sits alongside liquidity, fill rate (match rate) and market depth. Fill rate is the share of demand that finds supply and transacts.

items.wording: The customer clicked accept on the portal instead of signing paper. Is that binding?
items.answer: It can be. Under Federal Decree-Law No. 46 of 2021 on Electronic Transactions and Trust Services, electronic documents and signatures are valid when its requirements are met, and practitioners say a customer accepting a quote on the platform can form a valid contract. The platform's records are evidence, so they must be complete and unaltered: who accepted, when, which quote revision, and the exact terms shown. The law's signature assurance levels were not read at source and are not established here. For large orders, recommend a signed LPO or contract with an identified authorised signatory. The seat never alters a stored acceptance; corrections are new revisions.

items.wording: A client's CCTV quote lists a DVR, another lists an NVR. What is the actual difference?
items.answer: A DVR receives analogue video over coaxial cable and digitises and compresses it inside the recorder; each camera needs its own BNC input and usually separate power. An NVR receives already-encoded streams from IP cameras over Ethernet, so compression happens in the camera, and PoE carries power and data on one cable. IP scales beyond a fixed channel count, supports higher resolutions (4MP-12MP and 4K) and edge analytics, and integrates through ONVIF. HD-analogue is cheaper per channel and tolerates long coax runs but is capped in resolution. Hybrid recorders (XVR) mix both for phased upgrades. In the UAE most new commercial and SIRA-regulated sites are specified IP; DVR/XVR mostly appears in small retail, villas and retrofits. To compare, confirm channel count, incoming bandwidth (Mbps), HDD bays, maximum HDD size, RAID, and whether the model is on the authority-accepted list.

items.wording: A building owner asks why the addressable fire panel costs more than the conventional one. Explain.
items.answer: The sources do not give a price difference, so I will not quote one. What drives the cost: an addressable system puts every detector, call point and module on a shared two-wire loop with a unique address, so the panel shows the exact device, reads diagnostics, applies drift compensation, and runs outputs such as fan shutdown from programming instead of hard-wiring. Loops are usually Class A with short-circuit isolators, so one fault takes out only a section. Price is also driven by device count, voice evacuation, networking and above all fire-resistant cabling and containment. Manufacturer guidance says conventional suits small, simple buildings with few zones. For the owner, the device price gap matters less than cabling, labour and future flexibility, and the choice follows the approved fire alarm design. Ask for itemised bills of quantities to compare like with like.

items.wording: What does 316 have that 304 does not, and why does it matter by the sea?
items.answer: Molybdenum. Grade 316 (EN 1.4401) adds roughly 2-3 percent molybdenum, which lifts resistance to chloride pitting and crevice corrosion; 304 has none. The pitting resistance equivalent (PREN) is about 23.1-28.5 for 316 against about 17.5-20.8 for 304 (British Stainless Steel Association). By the sea this matters because chlorides attack: all the UAE's main cities are on the coast, so 316/316L is the minimum for exposed outdoor use in coastal cities and around pools, and ASSDA advises 316 within about five kilometres of the surf. 304 on seafront balconies is a common complaint. Pair it with a smooth finish and washing, since even 316 can tea-stain. PREN ranks grades but does not guarantee 'no rust'. The splash zone or seawater contact needs duplex 2205. Do not test grade with a magnet; use an EN 10204 3.1 mill certificate.

items.wording: What does a VRF system give that ducted splits do not?
items.answer: Individual control and capacity modulation across many rooms. A ducted split hides one fan-coil section in the ceiling and serves one zone from one thermostat. A VRF/VRV connects many indoor units (cassettes, ducted, wall) to one outdoor module; each indoor unit has its own control, the outdoor unit modulates capacity with inverter compressors, and heat-recovery versions can cool and heat at the same time. It suits villas, offices and hotels where zone control and limited outdoor space matter. The price of that is that it demands certified installers, pipe lengths and height differences within the maker's limits, nitrogen-purged brazing, and a refrigerant-leak assessment for small occupied rooms (ISO 5149 or EN 378). Ask the buyer to state the system type, otherwise quotes mix all three and are not comparable.

items.wording: Why does XLPE cable carry more current than PVC of the same copper size?
items.answer: Because XLPE is thermoset and tolerates a higher continuous conductor temperature, typically 90 C against 70 C for thermoplastic PVC, and a higher short-circuit temperature (250 C against 160 C). A higher permitted temperature means the same copper size can carry more current before it reaches its limit. XLPE also has better dielectric properties and moisture resistance, and gives more headroom against Gulf ambient derating. The procurement consequence is that a schedule sized on XLPE cannot be swapped for PVC of the same cross-section without re-checking current capacity, voltage drop and fault withstand. That substitution is a classic quote-stage trap, so the quote must state insulation, standard and voltage grade. The exact ampere figures per size are not established in my sources.

items.wording: Why does tempered glass sometimes break by itself years later?
items.answer: Usually nickel sulphide inclusions. Tiny NiS crystals trapped in float glass can change phase after tempering and expand slowly at ambient temperature, so a tempered pane may shatter spontaneously months or years after installation, a real risk on high-rise facades and overhead glass in UAE heat. The screening remedy is heat-soak testing to EN 14179-1: finished panes are held at around 290 C (plus or minus 10 C) for a two-hour hold so most panes with critical inclusions break in the oven, not on the building. It does not remove the risk fully; EN 14179 is based on a residual rate of roughly one breakage per 400 tonnes of glass. Heat-strengthened glass does not normally need heat-soaking. Specify 'HST to EN 14179-1 with cycle records' for facade, balustrade and overhead tempered glass; it adds cost and some lead time.
items.note: Four-times strength and small fragments not stated

items.wording: What is the difference between PE, FR and A2 core ACP?
items.answer: The core decides fire behaviour. PE core is essentially solid polyethylene: light and cheap but highly combustible, implicated in major tower fires including in the UAE, and not acceptable on building facades under the UAE Fire and Life Safety Code. FR core swaps most of the polymer for mineral filler (the mineral share varies by maker and is not established from the sources) and typically reaches B-s1,d0 under EN 13501-1. A2 core is roughly 90 percent minerals (one Civil Defence approved panel declares 90 percent) and reaches A2-s1,d0, limited combustibility. For super high-rise, high-rise, malls, schools, hospitals and assembly buildings the Code asks for A1 or A2-s1,d0. The label 'fire retardant' proves nothing: ask for the accredited classification report for that exact thickness and core, plus the Civil Defence listing. The supplier proposes and prices the final specification.

items.wording: Green MR board or cement board inside a shower?
items.answer: Cement board, or another proper wet-area backer, not green board. Paper-faced moisture-resistant 'green' board (EN 520 type H) is a damp-area product: the US IBC rule that UAE specifications often borrow prohibits it where there is direct water exposure or continuous high humidity, and over a vapour retarder in shower or tub compartments. Permitted shower bases are glass-mat water-resistant gypsum (ASTM C1178), fibre-cement sheets (ASTM C1288) and cementitious backer units (ASTM C1325). Cement board does not soften when wet; it is heavier, harder to cut, needs corrosion-resistant screws and alkali-resistant mesh tape, and costs more. Neither board is waterproofing, so showers still need a tanking membrane with sealed corners, drains and penetrations. MR board suits the rest of the bathroom. The consultant's specification governs and the supplier proposes the final system.
items.note: Fire rating belongs to the tested system not made

items.wording: Someone just paid to unlock a supplier. What does finance do next?
items.answer: First, confirm the Stripe payment; a reveal whose payment is not confirmed is not revealed. The charge should be exactly 3% of the selected quotation, nothing added for card, no VAT. Then four steps, all mine: retrieve the Stripe invoice and file it in the books (fn_accountant_files_reveal_invoice), back it up to Dropbox, make the invoice PDF visible in the customer's portal in the right tab, and hand the confirmation to the sales engineer, who tells the customer. I never email the customer myself; only customer_support sends email and WhatsApp.

items.wording: Do we add 5% tax on top of our unlock charge?
items.answer: No. QuotesDone is not VAT-registered, so the reveal fee carries no VAT. It is the founder's ruling of 14 September 2026. The Stripe invoice shows no tax rate and no TRN, the fee is 3% of the ex-VAT quotation base and nothing else, and nothing is added for paying by card. An unregistered person must never show VAT on an invoice, because anyone who collects an amount as tax must pay it to the FTA. This changes only when taxable supplies cross AED 375,000 over 12 months or are expected to within 30 days; we then file the registration within 30 days. After registration, the plan assumes 5% VAT is added on top of the 3% fee so net revenue is unchanged, but that is a pricing decision for the CEO, recorded before the first registered invoice.

items.wording: If a buyer pays with a credit card, do they pay extra, and who eats the processing cost?
items.answer: No, the buyer pays nothing extra. They pay exactly the 3% reveal fee, because Cabinet Resolution 66/2023 Art. 5(3) forbids adding an amount for paying by card, and the total is shown before payment. QuotesDone bears Stripe's fee as its own cost: 2.9% plus AED 1 on a domestic card, 3.9% plus AED 1 on other cards, plus the tax Stripe applies to its own fees. Revenue is recognised gross at the full fee and the processing cost is booked separately to 5000 Payment processing fees. There is no VAT either, as we are not VAT-registered.
missing: nothing is added for paying by card
items.note: no surcharge; QuotesDone bears 2.9% plus AED 1

items.wording: A quote comes in at a hundred thousand dirhams. What do we keep?
items.answer: On a AED 100,000 quote the fee is 3% = AED 3,000, charged to the buyer only, uncapped, with no VAT and nothing added for card. We keep AED 3,000 less Stripe's cost: on a domestic card 0.029 x 3,000 + 1 = AED 88, leaving AED 2,912; on another card 0.039 x 3,000 + 1 = AED 118, leaving AED 2,882. Our revenue is only the fee, never the AED 100,000, which is the buyers' and suppliers' deal, not QuotesDone's turnover. The model's average is about AED 395 per reveal, a planning figure. Customer revenue starts only from January 2027.
items.note: AED 3,000 fee; derived net figures are correct arithmetic

items.wording: A buyer lost their receipt. Where can they find it again?
items.answer: In their portal, in the right tab: after every reveal the accountant makes the Stripe invoice PDF visible there, openable at any time. The portal shows the PDF stored at filing time, not a live link, because Stripe receipt URLs expire after 30 days. Stripe's own customer emails are off, so the buyer's documents are QuotesDone-template documents issued by the accountant and delivered by customer_support.
items.note: Invoice PDF visible in customer portal, as required.

items.wording: Which seat lets the buyer know their card charge succeeded?
items.answer: The sales_engineer. It owns reveals and speaks for the payment: it tells the customer that a payment went through. The accountant runs the payment, confirms the Stripe charge, files the invoice and hands the confirmation to the sales engineer. The accountant never emails the customer itself; only customer_support sends email and WhatsApp, and it delivers the QuotesDone-template documents that the accountant issues.

items.wording: The boss okayed a refund yesterday. Can I process the other three pending ones too?
items.answer: No. One approval never covers unlimited refunds. Every refund needs its own CEO approval and is tied to one Stripe invoice, issued against that exact invoice ID. So yesterday's approval covers only that refund; the other three each need a recorded CEO approval before I execute. For each one I first ask Stripe what refunds already exist on that charge, so a retry cannot pay twice, and a refund can never exceed what was paid. A money-out action without a recorded approver, a Stripe pre-check and an evidence link is a control failure.

items.wording: If we give a buyer their money back, do we deduct the card fee?
items.answer: No. The refund is everything the customer paid for the reveal, which is the 3% Reveal Fee alone, since no card fee was added. QuotesDone absorbs Stripe's own fee: Stripe does not return its processing fee on a refund, so it stays a cost of the failed sale, booked separately. The refund goes back only to the original payment method and can never exceed what was paid. It needs CEO approval and is executed by the accountant against the exact Stripe invoice.

items.wording: After approval, how fast does a refund actually go out?
items.answer: Without waiting a cadence: the resilience step refunds runs every 15 minutes, so an approved refund is picked up at the next run. Before executing I check Stripe for existing refunds on that charge. The bank's side is slower: banks take 7 to 14 working days to show the refund to the customer. Approval itself comes first, from the CEO seat, never automatic and never the founder, and the database enforces that execution requires the CEO approval, that the amount is the fee paid, and that refunds never return more than was paid.

items.wording: Which ledger account takes the money we hand back?
items.answer: Refunds go to 4900 Refunds and credit notes, a contra-revenue account: Dr 4900 Refunds, Cr 1010 Stripe balance. If the revenue was not yet recognised, deferred revenue is reduced instead. The refund is the full amount the customer paid, which is the 3% reveal fee alone, since nothing is added for card and there is no VAT. The original Stripe fee on the charge stays as a cost to QuotesDone, booked to a separate expense account, never netted against the refund. The refund can only go back to the original payment method, never to a bank account supplied in a message, and it is executed against the exact Stripe invoice after CEO approval.

items.wording: The refund job crashed and restarted. Could the buyer be paid back twice?
items.answer: It should not, by design, but I verify rather than assume. Before executing any refund I ask Stripe what refunds already exist on that charge, so a retry cannot pay twice. A refund can never exceed what was paid, and every refund is issued against the exact Stripe invoice ID with a CEO approval, one approval per refund. The database enforces this through fn_refund_execution_requires_ceo_approval, fn_refund_amount_is_the_fee_paid and fn_refunds_never_return_more_than_was_paid. The refunds step runs every 15 minutes, so after the restart I check the charge's existing refunds, confirm the one approved refund actually succeeded in Stripe, not merely submitted, and only then book it. A money-out action without a recorded approver, a Stripe pre-check and an evidence link is a control failure I report to the CEO even if the amount was right.
items.note: Stripe checked for existing refunds before refunding; idempotent.

items.wording: A supplier ignored a paid unlock and we refunded the buyer. What can we bill the supplier?
items.answer: The non-response charge: the exact amount refunded (the 3% reveal fee), plus the payment processor's fee QuotesDone paid on it and could not recover, plus the administrative fee (AED 500; AED 250 for a supplier on Supplier Agreement v12 or earlier), plus simple interest from the refund date until paid (12% a year for v14 and later; 9% for v13 or earlier). The older wording of a flat 3% charge is superseded. It is recorded in its own revenue account 4200, recognised when the trigger has occurred and collection is probable, and no invoice goes out until the evidence bundle (accepted version and timestamp, trigger timestamps, notices) is complete.
canon: interest_from_refund_date: interest from the refund date

items.wording: For a supplier signed on version 12 of the agreement, how much is the admin charge?
items.answer: AED 250. The administrative charge is AED 250 for a supplier whose accepted Supplier Agreement is v12 or earlier; it is AED 500 for later versions. The interest for such a supplier is 9% per annum simple (12% applies from v14), plus the refunded amount and, per the terms accepted, the processor fee. I confirm the version and acceptance timestamp before invoicing.

items.wording: The supplier still has not paid us. Do we file a police complaint?
items.answer: No. An unpaid supplier charge is a civil or commercial debt. It goes to the Dubai Courts as a payment order (writ of debt), not to Dubai Police. The accountant issues the formal legal document, with stamp and signature, that the founder can file himself without a lawyer. Going to court is a CEO escalation. Before filing, a notice for payment must be served, at least 5 days under the law and 7 days from QuotesDone. Interest is 12% a year simple on Supplier Agreement v14 and later, never compounded.

items.wording: How much warning must the supplier get before we apply to the judge?
items.answer: At least 5 days: the Civil Procedure Law (Federal Decree-Law 42 of 2022, Art 144(1)) requires a notice for payment giving at least 5 days before filing. QuotesDone gives 7. After filing, the judge decides within 3 business days (Art 144(4)).

items.wording: The court issued the order. What is the deadline to deliver it to the supplier?
items.answer: The order is void if it is not served within 3 months (Civil Procedure Law, Art 146(2)). Once served, the supplier may file a grievance within 15 days of service (Art 147(1)). Arabic is the official language of the courts (Art 5(1)). Court steps are recorded with fn_accountant_record_court_step and tracked in v_accountant_recovery_ledger.

items.wording: Can late interest itself attract more interest?
items.answer: No. The interest is simple, never compounded (Commercial Transactions Law Art 88). The rate is 12% a year simple for a supplier on Supplier Agreement v14 and later, and 9% for a supplier on v13 or earlier, running from the refund date until paid, on the amount owed rather than on interest already accrued.

items.wording: A buyer told their bank they did not recognise our charge. What happens to the funds?
items.answer: That is a dispute, and the money is frozen while it runs. Stripe debits the disputed amount plus a dispute fee from our balance and holds those funds for the whole dispute. While it is open we cannot refund outside the dispute process, since refunding during a dispute can double-reimburse. We usually have 7 to 21 days, depending on the network, to respond with evidence, and the issuer takes around 60 to 75 days to decide, so the cycle is often 2 to 3 months. Our rule is to draft the response first, then CEO review, then submit. Accounting: move the amount to a disputed receivable and expense the fee. If we win, the amount is restored, but the dispute-received fee is not refunded outside Mexico. If we lose, no further money moves and the amount is written off to 5100.

items.wording: Why did a buyer get our receipt but nothing from Stripe?
items.answer: Because Stripe's own customer emails are switched off (Settings, Business, Customer emails, for Successful payments and Refunds). Customers receive only QuotesDone receipts on the QuotesDone template, issued by the accountant and delivered by customer_support. If a Stripe receipt ever does reach a customer, the setting was changed and I treat it as a control finding. Stripe receipt URLs on the Charge object expire after 30 days, so the portal shows the Stripe invoice PDF stored at filing time.

items.wording: Two sign-ups share a mobile number. What does finance look at?
items.answer: A shared mobile number is one weak signal, not proof; the company treats email as identity, and a phone may confirm but never select an account. I compare several attributes: normalised email, the same trade licence number or TRN, the same IBAN, the same card fingerprint in Stripe, shared device or IP, and near-identical addresses or document images. Licence number, IBAN and card fingerprint are strong; IP alone is weak. A cluster is not proof, since branches of one company legitimately have several users. I ask whether it is used to obtain something allowed once, or to evade a sanction. Output is a case with the linked accounts, attributes and benefit obtained; the CEO decides and customer support communicates.

items.wording: What behaviour suggests a vendor is trying to avoid paying our commission?
items.answer: The signals, strongest first: contact details exchanged before reveal in messages, attachments or quotation PDFs, including obfuscated or spelled-out numbers and text in images; a buyer repeatedly engaging one supplier's quotes then not revealing, or cancelling after revealing a competitor but not that supplier; a supplier with normal quote-to-reveal conversion whose post-reveal activity with a buyer disappears while the buyer's RFQs in that trade stop; RFQs withdrawn shortly after a supplier's clarification message; near-identical RFQs posted repeatedly then closed without reveal. Each signal alone is weak, so I score them together per buyer-supplier pair over 90 days and never accuse on one signal. Note the fee is the buyer's 3% reveal fee; suppliers pay no commission.
items.note: Lists off-platform dealing signals scored together and investigated.

items.wording: A vendor contacted the buyer directly before unlocking. What do we charge?
items.answer: It depends on what the supplier did. Sharing or soliciting contact details during the anonymised stages is AED 10,000 per incident. If the supplier takes the introduced customer off-platform, the charge is the higher of AED 20,000 or five times the fee, for 24 months from the introduction. The fee is 3% of the ex-VAT quotation, so five times the fee is 15% of the quotation, which beats AED 20,000 only above about AED 133,333. Examples: AED 50,000 quote gives 7,500, so AED 20,000; AED 300,000 gives 45,000. Each incident counts separately. I open a case with the terms version and timestamp, the introduction record and proof of the contact; enforcement is the CEO's decision. Income is recognised when collection is probable, otherwise on collection.
items.note: States AED 20,000 or five times the fee per incident for off-platform conduct

items.wording: I have a receipt from a software vendor. Where do I forward it?
items.answer: Forward it to expenses@mail.quotesdone.com. Only the mail.quotesdone.com domain can receive; an address at the bare quotesdone.com silently accepts nothing. That mailbox is the source of truth for costs. The accountant reads it daily and books every receipt, and a receipt whose amount is only in the email body still counts. Software is classified by what it is for, for example a software vendor to 6000 software and hosting, with the receipt read for vendor, period, currency and VAT. A receipt that cannot be read is held, never guessed.

items.wording: Some forwarded receipts from months ago are not in Resend anymore. Are they gone?
items.answer: No, they are not gone. Resend keeps inbound mail only about one month, so public.inbound_messages, which captures each message on arrival, is the durable record, and behind that is the founder's Gmail sent folder. A receipt with the amount only in the email body is still a receipt. If one genuinely cannot be read or found, it is held with a specific question and resolved by requesting a better copy from the vendor or matching to the bank or card line, never guessed.

items.wording: Our AI subscription does not appear on the bank statement. Problem?
items.answer: Not a problem by itself. The Claude and OpenAI company subscriptions (AED 799 a month each) were paid on the founder's personal card until early October 2026. I book them as expenses the owner paid on the company's behalf, from the receipts in the expenses mailbox, which is the source of truth for costs, and I never match them to the Mashreq statement until he says the card moved. They are founder-linked, so they are tagged as related party. If the card has moved and a charge still does not show, that becomes an unmatched line to chase until explained.

items.wording: The amount on a photo of a receipt is unreadable. Do we guess?
items.answer: No, we hold it, never guess. The held item records what is missing and the specific question (for example, amount unreadable, need a PDF invoice from the vendor portal). Resolution routes: request a better copy from the vendor, match to the bank or card line to recover amount and date, or for a small charge with clear vendor and nature book from the statement with the note no receipt, booked from bank line. Holds have an age limit: at month end I list them with age and value, and anything still held at close is booked on best evidence with a flag, or accrued, so the month is complete.

items.wording: How do we prove the money Stripe sent matches what landed in the bank?
items.answer: By a documented two-leg reconciliation. When Stripe creates a payout I move it from 1010 Stripe balance to 1020 Cash in transit; when the Mashreq statement shows the credit I move it from 1020 to 1000 Bank. I match by amount, currency and date window, using the payout reference where the bank narrative carries it. Each payout must also tie back to the balance transactions it settled, so revenue, fees and refunds inside it are all accounted for. The founder forwards the Mashreq PDF monthly and I import it. Because it is the same account Stripe pays into, payouts are matched to its credit lines and never treated as an independent second source. Exceptions listed at close: payouts in transit too long, bank credits labelled Stripe with no payout, amount mismatches, and failed payouts. 1020 should be zero or only recent payouts. In the audit, 0 of 1 payouts had been matched, so the first match must be proven before relying on the routine.

items.wording: Inside Stripe, which records do the books rely on?
items.answer: The books rely on Stripe balance transactions. Stripe creates one for every movement into or out of the Stripe balance, each with an amount, fee, net, currency, status (pending or available), type, reporting_category and a source ID. We classify by reporting_category rather than type. I import all balance transactions for the period and map each category to GL accounts: gross charge to revenue or deferred revenue, Stripe fee to 5000, refund to 4900, dispute amounts to receivable-in-dispute or loss, payout to cash in transit. The closing Stripe balance in the GL must equal Stripe's reported balance, and any unmapped category stops the close until it is mapped. Payouts are the balance transactions I match to Mashreq credits, and Stripe equals the books, reconciled daily.

items.wording: A supplier name hits the UN list. Should we just remove them?
items.answer: No. A sanctions match is banned and sealed, never deleted. The ban is append-only in the database, the sealed identity cannot re-register, and no notification can reach the party. Keeping the sealed record is what lets us prove later that we screened, refused and did not deal. A match goes to the CEO. Under the targeted financial sanctions framework, freezing applies without delay (within 24 hours), and reports are filed within five business days. A partial match suspends the party's money-out actions and new RFQ activity until disposition.

items.wording: Against which lists do we check suppliers every day?
items.answer: The UAE Local Terrorist List and the UN Consolidated List (4,396 entries on 28 September 2026: 618 local, 3,778 UN). I re-screen every registered or approved supplier daily (accountant.sanctions_rescreen) and every beneficial owner daily (accountant.ubo_rescreen). A stale list is itself a finding.

items.wording: The screen found a similar but not identical name. What now?
items.answer: A similar but not identical name is a partial match, not a clean pass and not yet a confirmed hit. Name similarity alone is never enough to confirm. I compare the list entry's identifiers (aliases, date of birth, nationality, passport or ID numbers, addresses, or registration details for entities) against our record (licence, UBO data, Emirates ID if captured). A mismatch on a strong identifier, such as a different date of birth or licence authority and number, supports a false positive, which I whitelist for that list-entry version only and sign off with evidence. If the identifiers cannot confirm or exclude, it stays a partial match: I immediately suspend money-out actions and new activity for the party, notify the CEO the same day and prepare the partial name match report. Freezing is expected within 24 hours and reporting within five business days. The party is not told why (no tipping off); customer support uses a neutral CEO-approved message, and the CEO signs off every partial and confirmed disposition.

items.wording: What does the CEO get from finance every week?
items.answer: A short, factual, decision-oriented weekly report with seven parts. (1) Cash: bank, Stripe available and pending, as-of dates, change on last week. (2) Revenue this week and month to date by stream (reveals, subscriptions, non-response charges) with refunds and disputes shown. (3) Costs month to date by account family against the prior month, flagging any new vendor or a charge more than 20% above its usual level. (4) Exceptions: unreconciled bank lines, held receipts, failed payouts or refunds, disputes with deadlines in the next 7 days. (5) Compliance: the next three calendar deadlines with status. (6) Risk: fraud and circumvention signals and sanctions or UBO re-screen results, with any partial or confirmed match as a separate headline. (7) Decisions needed, each with options and a recommendation. Every figure states its source and date, and an unmeasured number is flagged, never carried forward silently.

items.wording: The monthly bank PDF failed to parse. Do we ask the owner to send it again?
items.answer: No. An unreadable statement is our own defect, a reader fix for the it_engineer, and never a question to the founder (his words, instruction 384: if the agent cannot read it then fix it). Meanwhile the integrity rule holds: a statement that fails any check (source, continuity, arithmetic, account identity, duplicates, completeness of parsed lines) is held whole and nothing from it is posted. I archive the original PDF with its hash on arrival, because the inbound mail provider keeps messages only about a month.

items.wording: What is the monthly account fee at our bank?
items.answer: AED 199 a month plus AED 9.95 VAT, which is the bank's own VAT on its fee. That was measured on the August 2026 Mashreq statement. Because the company is not VAT-registered, both amounts are booked to 6300 General and Administrative, and the VAT is a cost, not recoverable. Bank interest of AED 0.86 on that statement goes to 7000 other income.
items.note: AED 199 plus AED 9.95 VAT.

items.wording: The owner sent five thousand dirhams to the company. Do we record a loan to him?
items.answer: No. Money the founder transfers in is capital unless he explicitly says it is a loan. I identify it by the sender IBAN and account name on the owner record, not by narrative text. Booking: Dr 1000 Bank / Cr 3100 Capital contributions, with the statement line ID as evidence. Only if he later states that this specific transfer was a loan do I reclassify to 2400 Owner loan, recording the date and his words. If the IBAN does not match, it is not assumed capital: it goes to a suspense line and is investigated. IBAN match with no loan instruction equals capital.

items.wording: What happens at the end of every month in the books?
items.answer: Month end runs as a fixed sequence with evidence at every step, and the target is the monthly close by day 5. I export all Stripe balance transactions to the last second of the month and import the Mashreq statement (the founder forwards the PDF to the expenses mailbox). Then I reconcile the bank to zero unexplained difference and the Stripe balance (opening + charges - refunds - fees - disputes - payouts = closing). Next I post reveals and subscriptions, deferred revenue, refunds and disputes, classify all receipts, post accruals and prepayment releases, and support every balance sheet account with a schedule tied to the GL. I do an analytical review against the prior month and budget, run the VAT threshold test, and close and lock the period. The pack to the CEO carries P&L, balance sheet, cash with runway, key variances and open issues. A step without evidence is not done.

items.wording: Can someone post a correction into a month that is already closed?
items.answer: No, not directly. Once a month is closed and reported, postings dated in that month are blocked, and the block is enforced in the database so every writer, including routines and scripts, obeys it. A correction goes in as a dated adjusting entry in the current open period, with a back-reference to the original entry. Reopening a closed period is the exception: it needs a recorded reason, records who reopened it and when, and produces a notice to the CEO. We reopen only when the error is material to a statutory output (financial statements or a tax return) that has not yet been filed. Entries are never deleted; errors are reversed and re-posted. This keeps figures already given to the CEO reproducible and the audit trail meaningful.
missing: postings dated in that month must be blocked
items.note: Blocked in locked month; adjusting entry in open period.

items.wording: How many months can we keep going with the cash we have?
items.answer: The number of months is not established in my knowledge here; no cash balance or burn figure was given, and I do not state one from assumption. The method is: spendable cash is the Mashreq balance from the latest reconciled statement plus known movements, plus the Stripe available balance (pending shown separately), less committed outflows due within 30 days. Burn is the average net operating cash outflow of the last three closed months, with fixed and variable costs split. Runway equals spendable cash divided by monthly net burn, with the assumptions stated. Owner capital is financing, not operating inflow. For going concern I need a forecast covering at least twelve months.

items.wording: Marketing spent nothing on ads this month. Is the ad reconciliation skipped?
items.answer: No, it is not skipped; it changes shape. Each month I confirm that no ad charges appear on the card or bank. If any do, I identify the account and campaign and raise it to the CEO as an unexpected charge, since it may mean a forgotten or unauthorised campaign, or card fraud. The marketing seat currently runs organic activity only, and paid campaigns are the founder's decision. When paid activity starts, marketing hands me the planned budget and campaign IDs before any spend, and I report actual against budget weekly and reconcile platform billing to card lines, with delivered-but-unbilled spend accrued at month end.

items.wording: How much do we set aside for renewing the eTrader licence?
items.answer: AED 1,200. The DET eTrader licence costs AED 1,200; the founder asked only that the number be noted. It is budgeted as a renewal fee in the monthly close, through fn_accountant_renewals_tick and fn_accountant_renewal_budget_line, so cash and runway already carry the cost before it is paid. The licence is typically a prepayment, released over the licence year. An unexpected charge, or a renewal above the budgeted amount, is escalated to the CEO. The TDRA NOL for quotesdone.ae (expiring 14 September 2027) is a separate renewal.

items.wording: When is our trade licence up for renewal?
items.answer: The trade licence, DET 1633275, expires on 24 June 2027 (issued 25 June 2026). Renewal work starts at least 60 days before expiry, because UBO and other filings can block renewal. Counting back 60 days from 24 June 2027 gives about 25 April 2027. The renewal is a company task due then, and the fee is budgeted in the monthly close.

items.wording: What turnover forces us to register for VAT?
items.answer: Mandatory VAT registration is triggered when taxable supplies and imports exceeded AED 375,000 over the previous 12 months, or are expected to exceed it within the next 30 days. I run both tests every month. The base is our own taxable supplies, meaning reveal fees, subscriptions and recoveries, not the gross value of quotations passing through the platform. Imported services we buy (overseas software and hosting) count toward the test, which can bring the crossing date earlier. AED 187,500 is only the voluntary threshold and is not our trigger. At 70% of AED 375,000, which is AED 262,500, on either test, I send the CEO a registration-readiness note. On crossing, registration starts immediately and the application is filed within 30 days, with the crossing date recorded.
items.note: AED 375,000; 70% = 262,500 is correct arithmetic.

items.wording: We just passed the VAT line. What is the deadline to apply?
items.answer: File the registration application within 30 days of the crossing; that is the seat's KPI. Mandatory registration applies once taxable supplies and imports exceed AED 375,000 over 12 months, or are expected to within the next 30 days, so on crossing I start the registration process immediately via the FTA's EmaraTax, record the date the threshold was crossed, and tell the CEO, since crossing the threshold is an escalation. The base is our own fees (and imported services), not the gross value of quotations. The statutory penalty for late VAT registration is not established in the sources I have.

items.wording: Should finance be running a corporate tax filing schedule?
items.answer: No. On 14 September 2026 the founder said to ignore the corporate tax matter (instruction 344), so the seat has no corporate-tax calendar, there is no CT duty in public.seat_duty and none should be built, and I open no CT tasks, reminders or deadlines on my own. The CT law entries stay as reference knowledge so a CT question is answered correctly. What instruction 344 does not establish is that any statutory CT registration or filing obligation is waived; a question that turns on that goes to the CEO with the law entries attached, not answered by assumption. For reference, the law itself sets the return and payment within 9 months of period end.

items.wording: What is in the annual accounts package?
items.answer: A complete, reproducible pack: statement of financial position, statement of comprehensive income, statement of changes in equity, statement of cash flows, and notes covering accounting policies and framework edition, revenue recognition and the principal/agent judgement, related parties including the founder, taxation with the CT computation and SBR election, significant judgements and estimates, events after the reporting date, and the going concern assessment. Supporting schedules: trial balance, every balance sheet reconciliation, revenue by stream, expense by account, fixed assets, deferred revenue, prepayments and accruals, owner capital and loan movements, and the tax bridge.

items.wording: Which things can finance decide alone?
items.answer: The accountant decides alone: booking, categorisation, the calculation of every document (refund, charge, invoice), and flagging fraud. A choice between two expense accounts is decided and noted. The accountant escalates to the CEO: every refund (for approval), a non-response charge reaching its legal stage, crossing the VAT threshold of AED 375,000, a mismatch where Stripe, books or bank do not agree, and an unexpected charge. Anything affecting revenue recognition, tax, the owner's accounts or unexplained cash is escalated regardless of size, and suspected fraud or a sanctions match is escalated immediately.

items.wording: Can finance write to a supplier directly about what they owe?
items.answer: Not by itself. Only customer_support sends email and WhatsApp, so the accountant calculates the amount, issues the document, and asks customer_support to deliver it. For receivables the path is a reminder at due date, a second reminder with amount and invoice at 7 days, a handoff to the sales engineer for a relationship call at 14 to 21 days, and escalation to the CEO for formal steps beyond that. Enforcement of a penalty, and going to court, are CEO decisions. Every handoff is tracked and closed by the accountant, and no receivable sits over 60 days without a named next action and date.

items.wording: How fresh must the books be, and when must the month be closed?
items.answer: Books must be current within 24 hours. Stripe is reconciled to the books daily, and every receipt is booked (the expenses mailbox is read daily). The monthly close KPI is by day 5: five working days from month end to period lock. After the close and lock, nothing posts silently into the closed month; late items go to the current period with a back-reference, and reopening needs a recorded reason and a notice to the CEO. A weekly finance report goes to the CEO with the date of each input so staleness is visible.

items.wording: How often is Stripe tied out to the ledger?
items.answer: Daily. The KPI is Stripe equals the books, reconciled daily, and the daily money duties run inside fn_accountant_duties (step accountantDuties, every 30 minutes, gated to at most hourly), which includes the stripe and bank steps. The Stripe payment is also confirmed at every reveal, and approved refunds run through the refunds step every 15 minutes. At each period close, Stripe balance, payouts and the Mashreq statement must be fully matched, with zero unexplained items older than the period. The monthly Mashreq statement import and full bank reconciliation follow at month end.

items.wording: When do we expect the first unlock income?
items.answer: Not before January 2027. From October to December 2026 the company registers suppliers only; customers launch in January 2027, so there are no reveal fees, refunds or non-response charges before then. Customer-side activity opens only after the supplier base reaches roughly 1,000. Until then the books hold costs, founder capital and bank interest. Once live, a reveal fee is recognised at the moment of reveal (point in time). The exact date of the first unlock is not established in my knowledge, and forecasts are scenario-based assumptions, not measurements.

items.wording: Who pays a subscription first and how much?
items.answer: Nobody among the first 1,000 supplier registrations: they are free permanently under the signed Supplier Agreement. Supplier 1,001 onward pays AED 1,000 a year, annually in advance. That is its own revenue line, separate from reveal fees: the cash is deferred revenue, released straight-line over the subscription year. When the first payer will arrive is not established in my knowledge, since it depends on registrations reaching 1,001.

items.wording: An income line appears in November 2026 although customers start later. What is it?
items.answer: Treat it as an anomaly to investigate, not income. Customers launch in January 2027, so until then the books should contain only costs, founder capital and bank interest. A revenue line before then is most likely a test-mode charge or a ZZ DEMO fixture. I would also check it is not bank interest (7000 other income) or founder capital (3100) posted to the wrong account. I trace it to the Stripe balance transaction or bank line, correct it by reversal and re-post, and report an unexplained one to the CEO.

items.wording: How do we decide which account a new bill belongs to?
items.answer: By what the cost is for, not by whether it recurs. I read the receipt (vendor, lines, period, currency, VAT), recall prior decisions for the same and similar vendors from the classification memory, and reason against the chart of accounts, choosing the most specific account. Then I decide the period treatment: expense now, prepayment or accrual. If confidence is low, or the item could be personal, capital or related-party, I hold it with a specific question. While we are not VAT-registered, the VAT is part of the cost and posts with it. A new vendor never seen before is also checked for authorisation. The final decision and any correction is stored as a new example.

items.wording: Where is the monthly bank fee recorded?
items.answer: Both parts of the Mashreq monthly fee, AED 199 plus AED 9.95 VAT, are booked to 6300 General and Administrative, because the company is not VAT-registered and so cannot recover the VAT. The chart of accounts also lists 6500 for bank charges generally, but the measured treatment on the August 2026 statement is 6300. Bank interest (AED 0.86) goes to 7000 other income. The statement is imported with fn_accountant_bank_statement_ingest and every line is booked and reconciled.

items.wording: A dollar ad invoice was paid. Which exchange rate do we use?
items.answer: Where the bank or card statement shows the actual AED debited, that AED amount is the booked cost, because it is the real outflow and already includes the bank's conversion. If a rate is needed without a statement (an accrual or month-end retranslation), use the Central Bank of the UAE published rate for that date, or 3.6725 for USD, given the AED peg to the dollar. Record the source and rate on the entry, and keep the original USD amount. Card FX fees charged separately by the bank go to bank charges, 6500, not to the ad cost.

items.wording: A vendor billed us again. Does finance reuse how it booked them last time?
items.answer: Yes, as precedent, but precedent informs and does not decide. I recall prior decisions for the same vendor and for semantically similar vendors from the classification memory, including the account chosen and who confirmed it, then reason about what this bill is for against the chart of accounts, because one vendor can sell different things. If confidence is low, or the item could be personal, capital or related-party, I hold it with a specific question. The final decision, and any human correction, is stored as a new example. An example contradicted twice by human correction is retired, and unreviewed examples carry lower weight than confirmed ones.
missing: remembers how each vendor was treated
items.note: Reuses prior vendor treatment as precedent, not decisive.

items.wording: What does Mashreq charge monthly and to which account? Answer in Arabic.
items.answer: تفرض مشرق رسوماً شهرية للحساب قدرها 199 درهماً بالإضافة إلى 9.95 درهم ضريبة قيمة مضافة (وهي ضريبة البنك على رسومه)، وذلك بحسب كشف أغسطس 2026. وتُسجَّل الرسوم والضريبة معاً في الحساب 6300 المصاريف العامة والإدارية، لأن الشركة غير مسجلة في ضريبة القيمة المضافة ولا يمكنها استردادها. أما فائدة البنك البالغة 0.86 درهم فتُسجَّل في الحساب 7000 إيرادات أخرى.
items.note: Arabic answer: AED 199 plus VAT, booked to 6300 G&A.

items.wording: Can we put our start-up tax losses on the balance sheet as an asset?
items.answer: Not by default. A deferred tax asset for unused tax losses is recognised only to the extent future taxable profit is probable, and for a pre-revenue company with no trading record that threshold is hard to meet. I recognise one only with written evidence of probable future profit; otherwise I disclose the unrecognised amount. Either way I track the losses in a schedule by period (generated, used, 75% cap applied, balance) for carry-forward.

items.wording: Our developers built the platform. Can we capitalise that cost?
items.answer: No, not as the default: under Section 18 of IFRS for SMEs (2015 edition) all expenditure on research and development of an internally generated intangible is expensed when incurred, unlike IAS 38. Developer time, hosting during build and AI tooling spent on building the platform are therefore expenses. Capitalisation only if the adopted edition permits and the CEO approves, which is not assumed. Not verified: whether the 2025 edition keeps this rule. Purchased, separately identifiable software licences are different: recognised at cost and amortised, where cost is above the capitalisation policy threshold (AED 2,500).
items.note: No; development cost expensed when incurred under S18.

items.wording: The owner put money in. Which part of the cash flow statement shows it?
items.answer: Financing activities, never operating. The founder's capital injections, and any founder loan drawn or repaid, are financing. Booked as Dr 1000 Bank / Cr 3100 Capital contributions. We present the indirect method. Reveal fees, subscriptions and Stripe fees are operating, and equipment or purchased software is investing. The closing cash must tie to the reconciled bank and Stripe balances to the fils before the pack is issued.
items.note: Financing, never operating.

items.wording: A dispute at year-end settled in January for a different amount. Do we change the year-end numbers?
items.answer: Yes, adjust. A dispute outstanding at year end and settled in January at a different amount is an adjusting event under Section 32: it gives evidence of a condition that existed at the period end, so the year-end amounts change. Non-adjusting events, which arise after the period end, are only disclosed if material. Before sign-off I review every transaction and correspondence up to the authorisation date.

items.wording: Subscriptions the owner pays on his own card: are they related party items?
items.answer: Yes. The founder is both owner and key management, so his transactions are related party transactions by definition, including expenses he pays personally on the company's behalf, such as the Claude and OpenAI subscriptions on his personal card, and their reimbursement. I book them as expenses the owner paid on the company's behalf and tag them as related party at the time of booking; the Section 33 note is built from those tags, never from memory at year end. The note gives the nature of the relationship, amounts and outstanding balances.

items.wording: How far forward must we look when judging if the company can continue?
items.answer: At least twelve months from the reporting date (IFRS for SMEs Section 3). The assessment is built on a cash forecast covering at least twelve months past the reporting date, listing committed costs (licence renewal, hosting, subscriptions, bank fees) against cash in hand. If any gap depends on the founder injecting capital, I obtain a written, dated statement of his intention to support the company. I sign the going concern basis only when forecast cash, including documented founder support, covers twelve months of committed costs; otherwise I disclose a material uncertainty. The 13-week forecast is the weekly working tool, not the assessment horizon.

items.wording: We changed our expected refund rate. Do we restate last year?
items.answer: No. A change in the expected refund rate is a change in accounting estimate, applied prospectively: current and future periods only. Only a change in accounting policy or a prior period error touches prior periods, retrospectively, and both need a written memo. So I classify first: policy change, estimate change or error. A locked period is never edited in place; any correction goes in the open period with the restatement shown where it applies.

items.wording: We are suing a supplier for an unpaid charge. Can we record it as income now?
items.answer: No. A claim we are pursuing is a contingent asset: it is not recognised, and disclosed only when an inflow is probable, and it is not income until virtually certain (IFRS for SMEs Section 21). The non-response charge is recognised in account 4200 only when the contractual trigger has occurred and collection is probable; if collection is doubtful it is recognised when collected, or recorded with a full impairment. Once we are suing, collection is clearly in doubt. Going to court is a CEO escalation, and the evidence bundle must be complete.
items.note: Contingent asset, not income until virtually certain.

items.wording: Below what interest expense does the interest cap not bite?
items.answer: Net interest expenditure (interest expense minus interest income) up to AED 12 million in a tax period is deductible in full, even if it exceeds 30% of adjusted EBITDA (de minimis, set by Ministerial Decision 126 of 2023). Above that, deduction is limited to 30% of adjusted EBITDA under Article 30 of the CT Law, and the disallowed part carries forward ten periods. It has no practical effect today: we have no borrowing and are funded by founder capital.

items.wording: When can we reclaim VAT on an invoice a customer never paid?
items.answer: Not today. We are not VAT-registered and charge no VAT on the reveal fee, so there is no output tax to reclaim. After registration, Article 64 of the VAT Decree-Law allows relief on a customer's non-payment only if all conditions are met: the supply was made and the tax was charged and paid to the FTA; the amount was written off as a bad debt in our records; more than six months have passed since the supply; and we notified the customer of the amount written off. It is claimed as an adjustment in the VAT return, and if the customer later pays, the output tax is repaid in that period. We would hold the write-off entry, the six-month date check and a copy of the notice on file. The exact wording after later amendments to Article 64 is not verified.

items.wording: If we make a profit next year, how much tax do we pay on it?
items.answer: Corporate Tax is 0% on taxable income up to AED 375,000 and 9% above it. Example: taxable income of AED 500,000 gives 9% x 125,000 = AED 11,250, before any Small Business Relief election. Note it is taxable income, not accounting profit, so the CT bridge adjustments apply (for example 50% of entertainment added back), and brought-forward losses can offset at most 75% of that period's taxable income. Return and payment are due within 9 months of period end. Whether we are a taxable person at all depends on our legal form, which goes to the CEO.
missing: 0% rate on taxable income up to AED 375,000
items.note: 0% to AED 375,000, 9% above; example arithmetic correct.

items.wording: The founder owns the licence personally. When must it get a tax number?
items.answer: If the business is run by the founder as a natural person, as with our sole establishment (DET 1633275, owned 100% by him), he becomes a taxable person only once turnover from business activity exceeds AED 1,000,000 in a calendar year (Cabinet Decision 49 of 2023), and registration is due from that point, not before. A juridical person such as an LLC must register whatever its turnover. No seat duty watches this threshold, because instruction 344 rules that the books raise only VAT. The accountant applies the juridical-person rule the day the business becomes an LLC. The late-registration penalty is AED 10,000.

items.wording: We missed the tax sign-up date. How bad is it?
items.answer: For Corporate Tax, the late-registration penalty is AED 10,000 (Cabinet Decision 75 of 2023 as amended). The FTA waiver removes it if the first CT return is filed within seven months of the end of the first tax period instead of nine (for a 31 December year end, by 31 July of the next year); paid penalties are credited back. The announcement gives no end date, so re-check the FTA news page. The penalty clock runs while we think, so I act the same day and report the cause to the CEO. Note instruction 344 does not establish that registration duties are waived. A late VAT registration penalty is not established in my sources.

items.wording: Our books end in December. By when must tax be filed and paid?
items.answer: For a 31 December year end, both the return and any tax due must be filed and paid within 9 months, by 30 September of the following year. This applies whether or not tax is payable. A late return costs AED 500 per month or part of a month for the first twelve months, then AED 1,000 per month; unpaid tax attracts 14% per annum applied monthly. To keep the late-registration waiver, the first return should be filed within seven months of the first period end (31 July). Instruction 344 means the seat opens no CT calendar on its own; any CT filing question goes to the CEO.

items.wording: Our turnover is small. Can we be treated as having no taxable income?
items.answer: Possibly, through Small Business Relief, but it is an election, not automatic. A UAE-resident taxable person whose revenue is AED 3 million or less in the period and in each previous period can elect to be treated as having no taxable income. It is available for tax periods ending on or before 31 December 2029 (Ministerial Decision 131). It is elected in the return, and CT registration is still required. Qualifying Free Zone Persons and multinational groups above AED 3.15 billion are excluded. Losses from SBR periods carry forward to later non-SBR periods. I test 12-month revenue against AED 3 million each period and document it.

items.wording: The accounts show a profit. Is that the number we pay tax on?
items.answer: No. Tax is on taxable income, which starts from accounting profit under IFRS or IFRS for SMEs and is then adjusted in a documented bridge: add non-deductible items (fines and penalties, 50% of entertainment, donations to non-qualifying bodies, owner distributions booked in the P&L, any founder payment above market value), subtract exempt income, adjust related-party transactions not at arm's length, apply the interest limitation if relevant, then relieve brought-forward losses up to 75%. Then 0% applies to the first AED 375,000 and 9% above. I never file SBR or a return without a written bridge, even when the answer is zero.
items.note: Starts from accounting profit with documented adjustments.

items.wording: I took a supplier to lunch. Can the company deduct all of it?
items.answer: No, not all of it. Article 32 of the CT Law limits entertainment, amusement or recreation of customers, shareholders, suppliers or partners (meals, accommodation, transport, admission fees) to 50% deductibility. In the tax bridge I add back the other 50%. The cost also has to be wholly and exclusively for the business under Article 28. While we are unregistered for VAT, the VAT we pay is a real cost and is deductible together with the expense.

items.wording: How do we prove a deal with the owner was priced fairly?
items.answer: By applying the arm's length standard of Article 34 of the CT Law: the result must be consistent with what unrelated parties would have agreed. The law names five methods: comparable uncontrolled price, resale price, cost plus, transactional net margin and transactional profit split. I keep a related-party register recording for each flow the terms, the amount and a short market-value basis (a comparable price or a cost-plus rationale). The founder is a connected person, so a payment to him is deductible only up to market value and if wholly for the business. If a flow is not at market value, I compute the adjustment in the tax bridge. Money he puts in is capital, identified by IBAN.

items.wording: When we turn profitable, can the old losses wipe out all the tax?
items.answer: No, not entirely. Under Article 37 of the CT Law, carried-forward losses can offset at most 75% of that period's taxable income before loss relief, so at least 25% of it remains taxable income, and the 0% band up to AED 375,000 applies after that. Losses also cannot be claimed if they arose before CT started, and Article 39 requires the same 50% ownership to continue, or the same or similar business after a change. I keep a loss schedule by period showing generated, used, cap applied and balance.

items.wording: A Dubai vendor charged us 5%. Can we claim it back?
items.answer: Not while we are unregistered. Only a VAT-registered person can recover input tax through a VAT return. Until we reach the AED 375,000 mandatory threshold and register, the 5% a Dubai vendor charges us is simply part of the cost of the item. We post the gross amount (net plus VAT) to the expense or asset account the purchase belongs to, and keep the VAT amount as a memo field on the expense record. We do not book it to a recoverable VAT input asset, which would overstate assets and understate expenses. When registration takes effect, input tax on costs incurred after the effective date becomes recoverable, subject to a valid tax invoice and business use. Whether any pre-registration input tax can be recovered depends on FTA rules we must check at that time rather than assume.

items.wording: After registering, what about tax on our overseas SaaS bills?
items.answer: Once registered, overseas SaaS, cloud, language-model and foreign-billed advertising are subject to the reverse charge (Article 48(1), with Article 30(2)). We declare 5% output tax on the AED value and, if the cost relates to taxable supplies, recover it as input tax in the same return, so the cash effect is usually nil but both sides must appear: the same amount goes in box 3 and box 10. Since 1 January 2026 no self-invoice is required, but the supplier's invoice and supporting documents must be kept. I tag every vendor with its country and whether it charges UAE VAT; a vendor that does charge UAE VAT is not reverse charged. Before registration there is no reverse-charge return, but imported services still count toward the AED 375,000 threshold.

items.wording: For tax, in which country is our service treated as provided?
items.answer: The UAE. The general rule (Article 29 of the VAT Decree-Law) puts the place of supply of services at the supplier's place of residence, which for QuotesDone is the UAE. A reveal fee or subscription sold to a UAE buyer or supplier is supplied in the UAE and would be standard rated at 5% once we are registered; today we are not registered and charge no VAT. A fee to a business established outside the UAE is not automatically outside scope: it is zero-rated only if the export-of-services conditions are met, with evidence on file. Whether our platform fees fall inside the Executive Regulation's list of electronic services, which has its own use-and-enjoyment rule, has not been established from a fetched text, so it is an open question to settle before registration.

items.wording: A buyer based in Oman paid a fee. Do we charge 5%?
items.answer: Not today, since we are not VAT-registered and charge no VAT on any reveal fee. After registration, the answer is not automatically no. A fee to a business outside the UAE is zero-rated only if the export-of-services conditions are met: the recipient has no residence in an implementing state, is outside the UAE when the service is performed, and the service is not directly connected with UAE real estate or goods. Our services connect buyers to suppliers for works in the UAE, so zero-rating may be argued to fail. Until a written analysis exists, such fees are treated as standard rated once registered, and zero-rating is applied only with evidence of the customer's non-residence, its location at the time of service, and a note on the real-estate exclusion. Whether Oman counts as an implementing state is not established in my sources.
items.note: No VAT today; zero-rating possible after registration only with conditions.

items.wording: After we register, how long do we have to send a proper tax invoice?
items.answer: Within 14 days of the date of supply. Article 65 of the VAT Decree-Law requires a registrant making a taxable supply to issue an original tax invoice and deliver it to the recipient, and Article 67 sets the 14-day limit. The invoice template then carries the words Tax Invoice, our TRN, the customer TRN where registered, a sequential number, date, description, amount excluding VAT, rate, VAT amount in AED and total; the full field list comes from the amended Article 59 at that time.
