Also check that OAI-SearchBot is allowed. Never buy links, place undisclosed paid articles or plant fake reviews. llms.txt is hygiene, not a lever.

items.wording: The accountant just told me a fee changed; how do we stop ChatGPT repeating the old number?
items.answer: We cannot force an engine, but we act the same day, because engines repeat what they last indexed and an old fee can linger for weeks. Update the fact register first; fees are owned by the ceo and accountant. Regenerate every page, schema block, llms.txt and FAQ that renders the fee on the same day. Update dateModified and the visible last-updated date. Request a recrawl through Search Console URL Inspection and ping IndexNow for Bing and Copilot. Update third-party profiles such as Google Business Profile, directories and social bios. Add a short dated changelog line on the affected page. Then re-run the GEO prompts that touch the fee after 2 and 6 weeks and log whether engines have caught up. If a third-party page is the one cited, request a correction there.
items.note: Register first, regenerate, recrawl/IndexNow, recheck at 2 and 6 weeks

items.wording: We want Google to show our text in the answer box at the top. How should we write that part?
items.answer: Write it for the snippet type. For a paragraph snippet, put the buyer's question as the heading exactly as they would ask it, then a direct definition of about 40-60 words right under it. The answer-first rule is 40-70 words with the entity name, the number and the condition, and it answers the literal question in the first sentence. Example: 'Comparing quotes on QuotesDone is free. You pay only if you choose a supplier and want to see who they are: a 3% Reveal Fee on the value of the quotation you choose (before VAT), charged once.' Use no pronouns that depend on earlier text and no conditional fact that turns wrong when quoted alone. Put data-nosnippet on partial fee explanations. Where we describe quotes, use the approved wording: a comparison report of the best three technical quotes, plus every other quote listed so you can choose any. Arabic gets its own parallel page in Gulf-formal Modern Standard Arabic. Owning the box is not guaranteed.
items.note: 40-60 word answer under question heading, snippet types, literal first sentence

items.wording: Sales wants us to launch something big for suppliers next week. What do we pin down before saying yes?
items.answer: I would not say yes before these are pinned down. First, the campaign needs one objective, one audience (suppliers only), one primary KPI such as verified suppliers per trade, and a stop rule. Second, any discount, free period, prize, draw or gift is marked 'permit check' and does not go live until the DET position is recorded with its source; whether such a mechanic needs a DET permit is not verified. Third, every claim must sit in the messaging house with a checkable proof point, and the supplier terms must be stated exactly: registration free permanently for the first 1,000 suppliers, then AED 1,000 a year, with no date. Fourth, paid amplification needs the CEO's approval and a budget line, and it must fit the approved monthly plan. If it uses Click-to-WhatsApp ads, the first reply, the pre-filled greeting and the recorded marketing opt-in must be ready. Inbound replies are routed under the community rules.
missing: one objective, one audience, one primary KPI and a stop rule
items.note: One objective, audience, primary KPI, stop rule

items.wording: I need a caption for a post about buyers getting three quotes they cannot compare. How do I structure it?
items.answer: Use Problem, Agitate, Solve, which suits pain-driven buyer content. Open with the pain in the first line: three contractors, three different scopes, no way to compare. Agitate in a short line, because that is how budgets slip. Then solve with an honest line about the product. Do not use the sample line 'get up to three comparable quotes', because it breaks the hard rule. Say instead: a comparison report of the best three technical quotes, plus every other quote listed so you can choose any. Never write 'only three shown' or anything implying other quotes are hidden. If you mention cost, state the fee condition next to it: comparing quotes is free, and you pay a 3% Reveal Fee only if you choose a supplier. A request needs an account, so never imply 'no sign-up'. Use one idea, short paragraphs and one CTA matched to the funnel stage, with hashtags at the end. Run the fact-register, claims and Arabic-register checks, and record the framework used.
items.note: PAS, one idea one CTA, fact register check

items.wording: A sound is blowing up on Reels this week. How do we judge whether to jump on it?
items.answer: Run the trend reasoning sequence and end with post, adapt or skip, with one line of reasoning. One, signal: exactly what is trending, where, since when, and the evidence. Two, fit: does it connect honestly to procurement, trades, suppliers or UAE business life? If forced, skip. Three, risk: religious, political, national-symbol and tragedy-related trends are excluded; check the origin and any controversy, and the audio must be licensed for commercial use (the platform's commercial music library). Four, rules: media standards, platform policy, no competitor mockery, never 'AI', no F&B. Five, timing: our calendar still forbids weekend and holiday posting, so skip rather than break it, and it must fit the approved plan or the allowance for reactive posts. Six, creative: our angle in the first 2 seconds, bilingual captions. Seven, measure against the account's median post, not the trend's viral examples. Approve or reject within 48 hours.
items.note: Fit, origin/sensitivity risk, 48h decision, licensed audio

items.wording: We missed Thursday's slot. Can I just push it out on Saturday?
items.answer: No. A missed slot is skipped, never back-filled onto a weekend. There is no posting on weekends or UAE public holidays, and the UAE working week runs Monday to Friday, so Saturday and Sunday are the weekend. Normal business posts go Monday to Thursday, with Friday morning only for light content. If the content is still worth publishing, rework it for a future approved slot in the monthly plan. Only approved items publish.

items.wording: How should next quarter's social plan be organised so it is not random posting?
items.answer: Build it from pillars and a monthly plan, not post by post. Fix 3-5 recurring pillars: procurement know-how, trade craft and cost drivers, proof, product and how-to, and community moments. The starting mix of roughly 35/25/20/10/10 is a hypothesis, adjusted by the scorecard. Build each monthly plan 4-6 weeks ahead. Every post line carries date and time, platform, pillar, persona, funnel stage, format, hook, framework, CTA, asset link, owner, UTM, hypothesis ID and compliance status. The plan goes to the ceo seat, then to the founder for one-shot approval on the first day of the month, and only approved items publish. Keep about 20% capacity for reactive and trend posts, judged by the trend reasoning sequence. No weekend or UAE public-holiday posting. Run tests as hypotheses with one primary metric, a fixed window and a stop rule. Feed social listening findings into the pillars. Remember that until customers launch in January 2027, campaigns target suppliers.
items.note: 3-5 pillars, monthly approved plan 4-6 weeks ahead, 20% reactive, repurposing implied in plan

items.wording: Can we just upload our TikTok videos to Instagram as they are?
items.answer: No, not as they are. Do not post watermarked TikTok exports. Render native versions for Instagram, because Instagram makes low-resolution, watermarked, muted or bordered reels less visible. Reels spec is 9:16 at 1080x1920, with text and faces inside the safe zone away from the bottom caption area and the right-side buttons. Keep captions or on-screen text on, as many watch muted. Re-hook, re-edit to the platform's spec, and adjust the caption and hashtags to Instagram, where a handful of relevant tags is advised. Re-upload natively with credit if the content is user-made, with written permission, instead of using screenshots.
missing: watch it all the way through

items.wording: Someone left an angry comment on our LinkedIn post. Should we delete it?
items.answer: No, do not delete it. Hide or delete only spam, abuse, hate, scams or personal data exposure; legitimate criticism is answered, never hidden. Classify the comment (complaint, question, sensitive and so on) and reply in a human tone in the reader's language. Name the next step, move any personal details to a DM, and never discuss account specifics publicly. Complaints and account issues go to customer_support via social.escalation, and when it is resolved, go back to the public thread if appropriate. Do not argue. A single complaint with low reach is Level 1 and is handled in normal community management. If more complaints appear or the post gains traction, it becomes Level 2, and the ceo and customer_support are told within 1 hour. A legal threat, media enquiry or regulator contact goes to the ceo.

items.wording: A visually impaired contractor says our posts are hard to use. What should we change?
items.answer: Work through the accessibility checklist, which is aligned with WCAG 2.2 AA. Give every image meaningful alt text in the post's language that describes its purpose, not 'image of', and use the custom alt-text fields on Instagram, LinkedIn, X and Facebook. Put accurate captions on video, reviewing the Arabic ones by hand instead of trusting auto-captions, and add transcripts for long-form. Keep contrast at least 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for large text, and never carry meaning by colour alone, so red/green quote comparisons also need labels. Keep text in images minimal and repeat the key message in the caption. Write hashtags in CamelCase, use emojis sparingly and never mid-sentence, use descriptive link text, set correct lang and dir for Arabic, and avoid flashing content.

items.wording: Can we use the UAE flag and a leadership quote in our National Day ad?
items.answer: Not as proposed. The leadership quote is out: never use the Rulers' images or quotes commercially. The flag needs care: the standards require respect for the state's symbols, so never alter the flag or emblem, and national symbols used commercially need permission. If unsure, hold the ad and escalate to the ceo rather than publish. Use the national colours respectfully, with no discount-style 'Union sale' copy for a B2B service. A safe tone is gratitude, such as a thank-you to the suppliers and contractors who build the UAE. The penalty table under Cabinet Resolution 42 of 2025 reaches up to AED 1,000,000 for the gravest categories, which include disrespect for the state and its symbols. National Day is 2-3 December, a public holiday, so the post goes out on the last working day before.
items.note: Media law, no political/religious content and ads identifiable/not misleading not made

items.wording: Is it OK if the blog posts are written by our assistant tool rather than a person?
items.answer: Yes, with conditions. Google does not treat machine-generated content as against its guidelines per se; content made mainly to manipulate rankings at scale is spam however it is made, so the test is helpfulness and originality. Every machine-drafted asset must pass the post quality checklist with each fact traced to the fact register, and a person must review it. The cross-family rule applies, so a model does not judge content its own family produced. Arabic is checked by a native reviewer before publishing. Add what a model cannot: our data, suppliers' real work, named expertise. Log the model, prompt version and reviewer for each asset. Never invent people, fake employees, fake testimonials or realistic images of real people. A post in a named person's name needs that person's approval each time. Follow each platform's disclosure tool for realistic synthetic content, and public text never uses the two-letter abbreviation for machine intelligence.
missing: not against its guidelines per se
items.note: Acceptable if helpful; review, register, disclosure, no fakes

items.wording: Our Facebook ad got disapproved and we do not know why. What usually trips B2B ads?
items.answer: The usual B2B triggers are these. First, landing page mismatch: the product in the ad must match what the page offers, so an ad about 'free quotes' that lands on a page describing a paid reveal without explanation invites rejection. Second, personal attributes: copy that implies the viewer's financial status, such as 'Struggling to pay your contractor?'. Prefer statements about the service, such as 'Compare verified fit-out quotes in one report'. Third, 'free' without the fee condition, which is also a misleading claim. Fourth, recruitment-style ads such as 'join as a supplier', which should be written as a business offer, not a job ad. Meta reviews mostly automatically, usually within 24 hours, and a rejected ad can be edited and resubmitted or appealed through Account Quality. Diagnose and fix the copy or page, never work around it with a new account, and log the ad with its landing URL and approval status.

items.wording: A complaint about one of our suppliers is going viral on X. What do we do first?
items.answer: First, treat it as at least a Level 2 crisis and tell the ceo and customer_support within 1 hour. If there is media coverage, regulator attention or a legal threat, it is Level 3: the ceo leads and all scheduled posts are paused immediately. Then follow the steps in order. Pause scheduled content and paid activity. Establish the facts internally and never speculate. Acknowledge publicly and quickly, within hours, even if the facts are pending: we are aware, we are looking into it, here is how to reach us. Move the individuals involved to private channels. Correct any misinformation once, calmly, with facts and sources. Apologise specifically only where we are at fault, with the fix. Do not delete criticism and do not argue. Never name a party or reveal quote amounts or contact details. Afterwards run a post-incident review and re-run the GEO prompts, because crises get cited by answer engines.

items.wording: The dashboard says 171 suppliers were invited. Is that the number to report?
items.answer: Not as it stands. An invitation counts only as an actual delivered message, shown by the outbox record, not by a status column, which is not a delivery record. So first confirm how many of the 171 were delivered; that is not established from what I have. Even delivered invitations are the top of the funnel, not the outcome. Report the funnel per trade: sourced, delivered invitations, registered, verified (all six items complete), activated (first quote on a real request) and retained. The 2026 funnel showed many invitations and near-zero registrations. The scorecard rule is to judge by the top tier, which is verified suppliers added, and a vanity metric never appears without an outcome next to it. Fix the biggest drop first.
missing: a status column is not a delivery record
items.note: Prioritising trades where buyers post and coverage is thin missing

items.wording: We are running one ad for everyone. Where should the link go?
items.answer: Do not run one ad for everyone. Never send buyers and suppliers to the same page. Split it into a buyer ad and a supplier ad, each with its own landing page and its own campaign. The buyer page states the job in the headline, for example 'Get comparable quotes for office fit-out in Dubai', and states the model: comparing quotes is free, and you pay a 3% Reveal Fee on the value of the quotation you choose (before VAT), charged once only if you choose a supplier and want to see who they are. Its CTA is 'Post a request'. The supplier page states the gain ('Receive requests in your exact trade'), the cost to the supplier plainly (no commission; free for the first 1,000, then AED 1,000 a year), and the CTA 'Register your company'. Both need message match with the ad, an Arabic twin page, and consent-compliant tracking.

items.wording: If a contractor messages us from an Instagram ad on WhatsApp, can we send him promotions later?
items.answer: Not on the strength of that chat alone. A Click-to-WhatsApp ad opens a 72-hour window from our first reply in which any message type is free, and he can be answered freely within the 24-hour customer-service window, but that is a pricing rule, not consent. A chat is not marketing consent. Transactional consent does not cover marketing, and marketing templates go only to people who opted in to marketing specifically, with the opt-in naming the business and recorded with timestamp and source. So ask for that opt-in explicitly, in a separate statement, then use marketing templates (always charged), each ending with a one-word opt-out that is honoured automatically. Also, any promotion offering a discount, free period, prize or gift is marked "permit check" and does not go live until the DET position is recorded. Also remember that QuotesDone gives no discounts of its own on its fee or subscriptions.
